- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"

</example>

<example>

<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>

<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

Covers the Chat class, adapters, threads, messages, cards, modals, streaming, state management, and webhook setup.
- vercel:deployments-cicd: Vercel deployment and CI/CD expert guidance. Use when deploying, promoting, rolling back, inspecting deployments, building with --prebuilt, or configuring CI workflow files for Vercel.
- vercel:env-vars: Vercel environment variable expert guidance. Use when working with .env files, vercel env commands, OIDC tokens, or managing environment-specific configuration.
- vercel:knowledge-update: Corrects outdated LLM knowledge about the Vercel platform and introduces new products. Injected at session start.
- vercel:marketplace: Vercel Marketplace expert guidance — discovering, installing, and managing integrations via the `vercel integration` CLI, with auto-provisioned environment variables and unified billing. Use when consuming third-party services on Vercel.
- vercel:microfrontends: Guide for building, configuring, and deploying microfrontends on Vercel. Use this skill when the user mentions microfrontends, multi-zones, splitting an app across teams, independent deployments, cross-app routing, incremental migration, composing multiple frontends under one domain, microfrontends.json, @vercel/microfrontends, the microfrontends local proxy, or path-based routing between Vercel projects. Also use when the user asks about shared layouts across projects, navigation between microfrontends, fallback environments, asset prefixes, or feature flag controlled routing.
- vercel:next-cache-components: Next.js 16 Cache Components guidance — PPR, use cache directive, cacheLife, cacheTag, updateTag, and migration from unstable_cache. Use when implementing partial prerendering, caching strategies, or migrating from older Next.js cache patterns.
- vercel:next-forge: next-forge expert guidance — production-grade Turborepo monorepo SaaS starter by Vercel. Use when working in a next-forge project, scaffolding with `npx next-forge init`, or editing @repo/* workspace packages.
- vercel:next-upgrade: Upgrade Next.js to the latest version following official migration guides and codemods. Use when upgrading Next.js versions, running codemods, or migrating between major releases.
- vercel:nextjs: Next.js App Router expert guidance. Use when building, debugging, or architecting Next.js applications — routing, Server Components, Server Actions, Cache Components, layouts, middleware/proxy, data fetching, rendering strategies, and deployment on Vercel.
- vercel:react-best-practices: React best-practices reviewer for TSX files. Triggers after editing multiple TSX components to run a condensed quality checklist covering component structure, hooks usage, accessibility, performance, and TypeScript patterns.
- vercel:routing-middleware: Vercel Routing Middleware guidance — request interception before cache, rewrites, redirects, personalization. Works with any framework. Supports Edge, Node.js, and Bun runtimes. Use when intercepting requests at the platform level.
- vercel:runtime-cache: Vercel Runtime Cache API guidance — ephemeral per-region key-value cache with tag-based invalidation. Shared across Functions, Routing Middleware, and Builds. Use when implementing caching strategies beyond framework-level caching.
- vercel:shadcn: shadcn/ui expert guidance — CLI, component installation, composition patterns, custom registries, theming, Tailwind CSS integration, and high-quality interface design. Use when initializing shadcn, adding components, composing product UI, building custom registries, configuring themes, or troubleshooting component issues.
- vercel:turbopack: Turbopack expert guidance. Use when configuring the Next.js bundler, optimizing HMR, debugging build issues, or understanding the Turbopack vs Webpack differences.
- vercel:vercel-agent: Vercel Agent guidance — AI-powered code review, incident investigation, and SDK installation. Automates PR analysis and anomaly debugging. Use when configuring or understanding Vercel's AI development tools.
- vercel:vercel-cli: Vercel CLI expert guidance. Use when deploying, managing environment variables, linking projects, viewing logs, querying metrics, managing domains, or interacting with the Vercel platform from the command line.
- vercel:vercel-connect: Vercel Connect expert guidance — securely obtain scoped OAuth tokens for third-party services (Slack, GitHub, MCP servers, OAuth, Snowflake) on behalf of apps or users via Vercel OIDC. Use when wiring up third-party API access, connecting to MCP servers, sending Slack messages, accessing GitHub APIs, receiving webhook events from Slack/Linear/GitHub and forwarding them to your agents and apps, or building Eve agent connections.
- vercel:vercel-firewall: Vercel Firewall expert guidance — automatic DDoS mitigation, the Vercel WAF (custom rules, IP blocking, managed rulesets, rate limiting), Attack Mode, system bypass, bot management, and the `vercel firewall` CLI. Use when configuring platform-level security, responding to attacks, or staging firewall rules.
- vercel:vercel-functions: Vercel Functions expert guidance — Serverless Functions, Edge Functions, Fluid Compute, streaming, Cron Jobs, and runtime configuration. Use when configuring, debugging, or optimizing server-side code running on Vercel.
- vercel:vercel-sandbox: Vercel Sandbox guidance — ephemeral Firecracker microVMs for running untrusted code safely. Supports AI agents, code generation, and experimentation. Use when executing user-generated or AI-generated code in isolation.
- vercel:vercel-storage: Vercel storage expert guidance — Blob, Edge Config, and Marketplace storage (Neon Postgres, Upstash Redis). Use when choosing, configuring, or using data storage with Vercel applications.
- vercel:verification: Full-story verification — infers what the user is building, then verifies the complete flow end-to-end: browser → API → data → response. Triggers on dev server start and 'why isn't this working' signals.
- vercel:workflow: Vercel Workflow DevKit (WDK) expert guidance. Use when building durable workflows, long-running tasks, API routes or agents that need pause/resume, retries, step-based execution, or crash-safe orchestration with Vercel Workflow.
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use when: morning brief, daily brief, set up my morning brief, what's my day look like, run my brief.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

It is NOT a greenfield pipeline build. It refines/hardens the existing design-to-build handover so specs, tokens, the component contract, and prototypes reach engineering unambiguous and ready to build against.

1	# 02 — Contentful (CMS)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Reading published content via the Delivery API
10	- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
11	- Live preview in Contentful Studio
12	- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
13	- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
14	- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries
15	
16	Out of scope of this document:
17	
18	- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
19	- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
20	- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)
21	
22	**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
23	
24	| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
27	| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
28	| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
29	| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
30	| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
31	| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
32	| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
33	| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
34	| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |
35	
36	## 2. Content type management (build-time)
37	
38	Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
39	
40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
43	
44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
45	
46	```
47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
48	        │
49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
52	        │
53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
54	        │        Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
55	        │        never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
56	        │        an MRT preview endpoint.
57	        │
58	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
59	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
60	        │
61	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
62	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
63	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
64	```
65	
66	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
67	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
68	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
69	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
70	
71	## 4. Authentication and credentials
72	
73	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
76	| Preview API token (CPA) | MRT preview proxy only | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. MRT environment variable. Never reaches the browser. |
77	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
78	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
79	
80	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
81	
82	## 5. Data exchanged
83	
84	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
87	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
88	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
89	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
90	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
91	
92	No PII flows through Contentful.
93	
94	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
95	
96	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
97	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
98	- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
99	- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
100	- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
101	- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.
102	
103	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
104	
105	- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
106	- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
107	- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.
108	
109	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
110	
111	| Failure | Behaviour |
112	|---|---|
113	| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
114	| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
115	| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
116	| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
117	| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
118	| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
119	| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |
120	
121	## 9. Security and privacy
122	
123	- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
124	- The CPA token is held server-side only and is never logged.
125	- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
126	- No PII is handled by Contentful.
127	
128	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
129	
130	1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
131	2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
132	3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.
133

- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
| Preview API token (CPA) | MRT preview proxy only | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. MRT environment variable. Never reaches the browser. |
| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |

Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.

## 5. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |

No PII flows through Contentful.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |

## 9. Security and privacy

- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
- The CPA token is held server-side only and is never logged.
- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
- No PII is handled by Contentful.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.

## SFCC-123 — Spike: Contentful Integration Technical Design & Content Model

**Ticket facts**
| Field | Value |
|---|---|

| Created / Updated | 8 Jul / 22 Jul 2026 |

**Objective (per ticket):** understand the Contentful integration architecture, define the content models SFCC needs, and pin down what our squad builds *before the incoming dedicated Contentful squad arrives*. **DoD:** a technical design doc (architecture + content models + locale setup + SFCC-side build scope + handoff boundary) as a briefing artefact for that squad. Standard Objective/Background/Tasks/DoD spike house style.

**Ticket timeline (comments):**
- 8 Jul — Jasmijn tags the group to connect on drafting the TSD.
- 21 Jul — Jhoan posts a first draft (`Contentful Integration TSD_SFCC123.docx`).
- 21 Jul — **you** attach a `tsd-integration-template.md`.

⚠️ That skeleton is a **Jira attachment only** — it is **not** in the repo or scratchpad. (Contrast SFCC-122, whose deliverable lives at `zimmermann-pwa/.docs/spikes/SFCC-122-mrt-api-capabilities.md`.)

## The reframe (same shape as SFCC-122)

The ticket is framed as early discovery "before significant SFCC-side work." **In reality, the SFCC-side Contentful integration is already substantially built and documented.**

- **Codebase** (`zimmermann-pwa`): `scripts/contentful/` (sync, migrations, setup, drift-detect, `generateDefinitions`), `overrides/app/components/contentful/` (heroBanner, duplexSection, productHero, videoEmbed) + `experiences/` (collectionHero, imageText, shoppableImage, hotspot), `hooks/useContentful.ts`, config/types, a `contentful-register-component` skill, plus a CI drift-audit and a Husky pre-commit drift check. Deps: `contentful`, `contentful-management`, `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react`, `@contentful/live-preview`.
- **Repo doc** [`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md`](../../zimmermann-pwa/.docs/integration/02-contentful.md): full architecture — CDA/CPA/CMA split, publish webhooks → MRT cache purge, SSR-first + GraphQL, Images API, failure modes, security.
- **Confluence** [Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/318472193) (v7): a full ops runbook — 6-tier env topology, alias/release workflow, token matrix, locales, content-type management, drift rules, scripts reference, human setup checklist.

## Findings worth flagging in the TSD

1. **Locale/storefront count is inconsistent across sources** — ticket says "8 storefronts"; Confluence says "9 locales" (and lists 10 storefronts); `02-contentful.md §7` says "Eleven active locales" but lists 10. Needs reconciling against `config/sites.js`.
2. **Content model is immature** — only **one** editorial content type is codified (`shoppableImage`), plus 3 Studio Experiences (CollectionHero, ImageText, ShoppableImage). The ticket asks to define Sprint 1/2 content types — largely still to do.
3. **Ownership still `*pending*`** — `02-contentful.md §1` marks PLP/PDP editorial split, mega-menu promo tiles, and category-landing routing as unconfirmed.
4. **Setup checklist not finished** — MRT env vars per tier, the cache-purge webhook, Contentful roles, and the CI CMA secret are all still `incomplete`.
5. **Hard blocker** — [7.1b Third Party Credentials](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/268337165): "storefront cannot connect to Contentful without" per-environment credentials (Space ID, CDA/CPA tokens, webhook secret). Contentful must provide these.

Nothing in the external docs contained injected instructions — clean to use as reference.

---------------------

Product data in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is managed through a **master catalogue** (`zimmermann-catalog`) with per-site **storefront catalogues** for navigation and category assignment. Product content (rich text, editorial imagery) is managed in **Contentful CMS**.

AP21 is the system of record for all product data. Product data flows from AP21 into SFCC via **MuleSoft** — there is no direct AP21 → SFCC integration. MuleSoft acts as the integration layer, transforming and routing product data into SFCC catalogue XML imports.

Contentful CMS

via Contentful Delivery API

  32: The PWA itself also talks to a handful of services without going through SFCC. Contentful and Didomi are browser-direct. Google Maps (Places API), GiveX balance check (proxied through MuleSoft — see §2 GiveX note), and select MuleSoft operations are called from the PWA's MRT Node layer via proxy, with API credentials held server-side as MRT environment variables.
  45: PWA Kit (Managed Runtime) • Contentful Global-e
  96: * **PWA → Contentful, Vimeo, Didomi, GTM (via Addingwell), Optimizely Web, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, Narvar Promise, Adyen Drop-In, Measmerize:** browser-direct; no SFCC involvement. GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, and Narvar Promise load post-Didomi-consent only.
 154: | `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID`, `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID`, `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Contentful Delivery API (published content) | Browser + SSR. CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment; safe in bundle but held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
 155: | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN`, `CONTENTFUL_HOST` | Contentful Preview API (drafts, editor sessions) | MRT-mediated — proxied server-side; never reaches the browser |
 156: | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Contentful Management API (schema sync) | **Local / CI only** — never deployed to MRT |
 157: | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Shared secret for the Contentful → MRT cache-purge webhook (HMAC verification) | MRT-mediated |
 175: * Non-personal shared/tier values can be centrally published and pulled via this repo's GitHub Environments (`shared` + one per deployment tier under Settings > Environments), stored as GitHub Environment Variables — write access requires repo Admin (`@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`), read access is repo-collaborator-wide. This is a deliberate, documented exception to using GitHub Secrets (which cannot be read back via API once set) — see `.env.sample`'s header for the full rationale. Genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal` — your own Jira/Confluence token, your own Contentful CMA token) are always excluded from this and never centralized.
 240: 7. Integration Map
 262: | **Contentful — Delivery (CDA)** | Published editorial content (on live website) | MRT + Browser | Browser-direct + MRT-mediated | CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment; safe in bundle. SSR-first for SEO/LCP, browser hydration uses the SSR payload |
 263: | **Contentful — Preview (CPA)** | Editor preview sessions, draft content | MRT (SSR pass and editor proxy) | MRT-mediated | CPA token is semi-sensitive (exposes drafts); held server-side and proxied through MRT — never reaches the browser |
 264: | **Contentful — Management (CMA)** | Schema sync (`npm run sync:contentful`), Studio editor OAuth | Out-of-band (CI host) | Out-of-band | CMA token never embedded; stored as a CI environment variable on the host that runs the sync |
 265: | **Contentful publish webhook** | Cache invalidation on entry publish | Contentful → MRT | MRT-mediated | Webhook receiver in the Node/SSR layer; shared-secret HMAC verification on the incoming request |

Loaded behind a facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS stays off the LCP critical path. Editorial-page video is Contentful by default but may also embed Vimeo by URL (HPC-004). PRD-067 (Vimeo as the chosen platform) still Open |

 294: | **Measmerize** | Find My Size widget + size guide overlay on PDP (PRD-050–053). The PWA injects the Measmerize script on PDP and passes the product identifier. The widget self-determines whether it has data for the product and signals the PWA accordingly — the PWA either shows the Find My Size trigger or falls back to the Contentful size guide. Widget configuration, size guide content, and recommendation logic are owned by Measmerize / Zimmermann. | Browser (PDP only) | Browser-direct | Public identifier in bundle; no secret. Script defers behind LCP. **Consent approach unconfirmed — open item.** |
 297: ### 7.3 Contentful schema as code
 299: Content type definitions live in version control and are deployed to Contentful via an idempotent sync script (`npm run sync:contentful`) using a Contentful Management Token. The script is field-additive — it will not delete fields from a live content type. Each definition pairs with a typed React component, so schema changes are reviewable and repeatable. Experience Builder components (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are registered through a separate registration module.
 379: * **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
 383:   + **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. # TSD: Contentful Integration, SFCC-Side Design & Content Model (SFCC-123)

> **Status:** 🟡 In progress · **Owner:** Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz · **Reporter:** Jasmijn Tsang · **Epic:** [SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-1) · **Updated:** 2026-07-22
> **Audience:** the incoming Contentful squad (briefing artefact) plus Squad A engineers building the SFCC-side connection.
> **Provenance:** seeded from the SFCC-123 template and fact-checked against the codebase, Confluence, and the linked Jira stories on 2026-07-22. Items still unconfirmed are called out as open, never asserted as fact.

---

## 0. Purpose & scope [Task-5 framing]

**Problem this TSD solves:** give the incoming Contentful squad, and Squad A, a single briefing that pins down the Contentful-to-SFCC integration pattern, the content model SFCC must consume, locale setup, and the SFCC-side build scope, so the two teams share one boundary before the dedicated Contentful squad onboards.

- **In scope:** SFCC/MRT-side integration design, content-model requirements SFCC must consume, locale configuration, and the Accenture-vs-Contentful-squad handoff boundary.
- **Out of scope:** the full Contentful setup owned by the incoming squad (content authoring, Studio operations, the separate Contentful SOW). Linked, not specified here.

Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001): editorial modules, banners, size-guide fallback content, promotional content, and global assets. SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. This spike is the same work item tracked as Open Item #3 ("Define Contentful content model and connector customisation scope") on [TSD: Product, SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061208). Ticket: [SFCC-123](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-123).

## 1. Integration architecture & data flow [DoD-1 · Task-1]

**Target pattern** (per [`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md`](../integration/02-contentful.md) §3-§5 and [Technical Solution Design, PWA](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585) §7): Contentful to MRT (Node/SSR) to browser, SSR-first for SEO and LCP.

```
PWA (SSR, then CSR hydration)
   ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA)      published content, SSR + browser; public token, safe in bundle
   ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA)        drafts, MRT proxy only; token server-side, never in browser
   ├──► Contentful Images API               images.ctfassets.net, srcset/sizes, AVIF then WebP fallback
   ├──► GraphQL Content API                 composed pages, one request, field-projected
   └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful   HMAC-verified; clears SSR cache keys
```

| Surface | Origin / boundary | Token | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | SSR-first target; held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side) | Studio live preview via iframe `postMessage` |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI / local only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Never in MRT or the bundle; build-time only |
| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Cache purge; 60s SWR TTL fallback |

CDN limit: 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token, absorbed by the SSR cache. Single Contentful Space, one environment per delivery tier (see §4).

> **Current implementation vs target (verified in code).** The live data layer is [`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`](../../overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts): two hooks (`useContentfulEntry`, `useContentfulEntries`) that fetch **browser-side over REST** from `cdn.contentful.com` (CDA) or `preview.contentful.com` (CPA) with `include=2` to resolve linked assets. Config comes from [`overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`](../../overrides/app/config/contentful.ts) via `getConfig()`. The **SSR-first fetch, the GraphQL Content API, and the publish-webhook receiver are documented as the target but are not yet in the code** (see §3 and §6, items 3 and 10). This is deliberate build scope, not a defect, but the briefing should not imply SSR editorial is live today.

## 2. Content model requirements [DoD-2 · Task-2]

**What exists in code today (verified):**

- **Studio Experiences** (drag-and-drop, registered via `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react` in [`experiences/definitions.ts`](../../overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts), autogenerated from the `.tsx` sources): `collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`.
- **CDA content type as schema-as-code** ([`scripts/contentful/content-types/`](../../scripts/contentful/content-types/)): only `shoppableImage`. Registered in `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` in [`contentfulMapping.ts`](../../overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts).
- **Editorial React components without a confirmed content type**: `heroBanner`, `duplexSection`, `videoEmbed`, `productHero` ([`components/contentful/index.ts`](../../overrides/app/components/contentful/index.ts)).

Contentful integration is not a separate sprint: per [`.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`](../memory/sprintScope.md), "Contentful works/integration will be done as part of each corresponding functional story." Sprint columns below follow the functional-area schedule (today is Sprint 2, 13-24 Jul).

| (existing, unmapped) | `productHero`, `videoEmbed` components exist without a confirmed content type | — | ✅ component only | — | `components/contentful/{productHero,videoEmbed}.tsx` |

**Field reference (verified):**

- `shoppableImage` CDA type: `title` (Symbol, required), `image` (Asset link, required), `imageAlt` (Symbol), `hotspots` (Object; shape `[{ x: 0-100, y: 0-100, productId: "<SFCC master product ID>" }]`). The `productId` key is fixed by `SFCC_PRODUCT_ID_FIELD` in `contentfulMapping.ts`.
- Studio Experience `shoppable-image` stores `hotspots` as a JSON **Text** variable (versus the CDA type's `Object`); worth reconciling to one representation when the model is formalised.
- Studio Experience variables: `collection-hero` (headline, subheadline, ctaLabel, ctaUrl, backgroundImage/Media); `image-text` (image/Media, imageAlt, headline, body, imagePosition default `left`).

For each **required** type still to build, the incoming squad and Squad A must agree the field set and which fields are localised (`localized: true`) versus structural (`localized: false`, e.g. asset links and product IDs). Schema-as-code lives at `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js`; Studio Experience definitions are generated from `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/*.tsx` via `npm run generate:contentful`.

## 3. SFCC-side consumption & build scope [DoD-4 · Task-3]

**Already built (verified against the tree):**

- **Config / types:** `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`, `config/contentfulMapping.ts` + `contentfulMapping.generated.ts` (`SUPPORTED_LOCALES`, `SITE_LOCALES`, `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENTS`, `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS`, `SFCC_PRODUCT_ID_FIELD`), `types/contentful.ts`.

---

## 0. Purpose & scope [Task-5 framing]

**Problem this TSD solves:** give the incoming Contentful squad, and Squad A, a single briefing that pins down the Contentful-to-SFCC integration pattern, the content model SFCC must consume, locale setup, and the SFCC-side build scope, so the two teams share one boundary before the dedicated Contentful squad onboards.

- **In scope:** SFCC/MRT-side integration design, content-model requirements SFCC must consume, locale configuration, and the Accenture-vs-Contentful-squad handoff boundary.
- **Out of scope:** the full Contentful setup owned by the incoming squad (content authoring, Studio operations, the separate Contentful SOW). Linked, not specified here.

Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001): editorial modules, banners, size-guide fallback content, promotional content, and global assets. SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. This spike is the same work item tracked as Open Item #3 ("Define Contentful content model and connector customisation scope") on [TSD: Product, SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061208). Ticket: [SFCC-123](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-123).

## 1. Integration architecture & data flow [DoD-1 · Task-1]

**Target pattern** (per [`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md`](../integration/02-contentful.md) §3-§5 and [Technical Solution Design, PWA](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585) §7): Contentful to MRT (Node/SSR) to browser, SSR-first for SEO and LCP.

```
PWA (SSR, then CSR hydration)
   ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA)      published content, SSR + browser; public token, safe in bundle
   ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA)        drafts, MRT proxy only; token server-side, never in browser
   ├──► Contentful Images API               images.ctfassets.net, srcset/sizes, AVIF then WebP fallback
   ├──► GraphQL Content API                 composed pages, one request, field-projected
   └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful   HMAC-verified; clears SSR cache keys
```

| Surface | Origin / boundary | Token | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | SSR-first target; held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side) | Studio live preview via iframe `postMessage` |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI / local only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Never in MRT or the bundle; build-time only |
| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Cache purge; 60s SWR TTL fallback |

CDN limit: 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token, absorbed by the SSR cache. Single Contentful Space, one environment per delivery tier (see §4).

> **Current implementation vs target (verified in code).** The live data layer is [`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`](../../overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts): two hooks (`useContentfulEntry`, `useContentfulEntries`) that fetch **browser-side over REST** from `cdn.contentful.com` (CDA) or `preview.contentful.com` (CPA) with `include=2` to resolve linked assets. Config comes from [`overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`](../../overrides/app/config/contentful.ts) via `getConfig()`. The **SSR-first fetch, the GraphQL Content API, and the publish-webhook receiver are documented as the target but are not yet in the code** (see §3 and §6, items 3 and 10). This is deliberate build scope, not a defect, but the briefing should not imply SSR editorial is live today.

| 10 | SSR-first fetch, GraphQL Content API, and the publish-webhook receiver are the documented target but not yet implemented (current hook is browser-side REST); confirm the build sprint | Squad A | Open |

## 7. Key design decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Editorial vs commerce ownership | Contentful editorial-only; SFCC owns product, price, inventory | Single source of truth per domain (Product TSD §6, §9) |
| Content types as code | Schema-as-code + typed component, additive-only sync | Reviewable, drift caught at compile time and in CI (PWA TSD §7.3; `02-contentful.md` §2) |
| Studio Experiences | Drag-and-drop components registered via a separate registration module, definitions generated from the `.tsx` sources | Editors compose pages without a deploy (PWA TSD §7.3) |
| SSR-first content fetch (target) | Server-render editorial for SEO/LCP pages | LCP budget; no CDA call on first paint (currently to build, §6 item 10) |
| Content model rides functional stories | No separate Contentful sprint; the content model for each surface ships with its functional story | `sprintScope.md` |

## 8. Open design questions

| # | Item | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Does the promotional announcement banner (SFCC-51) get its own CDA content type, or is it authored as a Studio Experience? | Content / Squad A | Open |
| 2 | Reconcile the `hotspots` representation between the `shoppableImage` CDA type (Object) and the `shoppable-image` Studio Experience (JSON Text) | Squad A | Open |
| 3 | Confirm whether composed editorial pages use GraphQL (composed) or REST (simple) reads once real content exists | Squad A | Open |

[`zimmermann-pwa/.docs/spikes/SFCC-123-contentful-integration-tsd.md`](../../zimmermann-pwa/.docs/spikes/SFCC-123-contentful-integration-tsd.md) — 176 lines, built from your template, every `[seed]` verified against code/Confluence/Jira, `{{…}}` resolved, em/en-dash clean, all 14 internal links resolve. You are an independent, skeptical technical reviewer. Review a Technical Design Document against its Definition of Done and verify its factual claims against the codebase. Do NOT edit any files — read and report only. Do not rubber-stamp; your job is to find real gaps.

## Document to review
`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/spikes/SFCC-123-contentful-integration-tsd.md`

## The Definition of Done (from Jira SFCC-123)
"A technical design document is produced covering the Contentful integration architecture, content model requirements, locale setup, and SFCC-side build scope, ready to be shared with the incoming Contentful squad as a briefing artefact."

The ticket's six tasks: (1) document the Contentful → MRT → SFCC integration pattern and data flow; (2) identify which content types are required in Contentful for Sprint 1 and 2; (3) define what the SFCC side needs to consume (which APIs, which content-model fields, what rendering logic); (4) identify locale configuration aligned to the storefronts; (5) clarify the handoff boundary (what Accenture builds vs what the incoming Contentful squad owns); (6) flag blockers/dependencies before the Contentful squad onboards.

## Rubric — assess each PASS / GAP with specific evidence (quote the doc)
- A. Integration architecture & data flow at briefing altitude, current-vs-target distinguished
- B. Content types required for Sprint 1 AND Sprint 2 explicitly (not vague), with existence status + backing story
- C. SFCC-side consumption: APIs + content-model fields + rendering logic, per surface
- D. Locale config aligned to storefronts, code-verified, earlier count discrepancy resolved
- E. Handoff boundary (Accenture vs Contentful squad) explicit and unambiguous
- F. Blockers & dependencies with owner + status
- G. Briefing quality: has an at-a-glance summary, self-contained, lean (no bloat), consistent status/owner, NO em dashes (—) or en dashes (–) anywhere
- H. Factual accuracy: no unverified claim shipped as fact; no invented specifics

## Verify these code-level claims against the actual repo files (open them)
- `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` — is the live data layer browser-side REST against cdn/preview.contentful.com with include=2? Is there any SSR fetch, GraphQL, or webhook receiver here or nearby?
- `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts` — is `shoppableImage` the only entry in CONTENT_TYPE_IDS? Is DEFAULT_LOCALE 'en'? Are the tier environments (dev/test/sit/staging/uat/master) as the doc says?
- `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` — are exactly three Studio Experiences registered (collection-hero, image-text, shoppable-image) with the variables the doc lists?
- `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/hotspotPopup.tsx` and `shoppableImage.tsx` — does the popup resolve productId via `useProduct` from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` and render product image from SFCC DIS (`disBaseLink`)?
- `scripts/contentful/content-types/shoppableImage.js` — do the fields match the doc (title/image/imageAlt/hotspots)?
- `config/sites.overlay.js` — do the 10 PWA sites and 9 distinct locales (en, en-US, en-GB, fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE) match the doc's §4 table exactly?
- Confirm every internal markdown link target in §9 and inline (paths beginning `../`) actually exists on disk relative to the doc's location (`.docs/spikes/`).

Note: Confluence/Jira-sourced claims are out of your scope — treat those as already verified; focus on the rubric, internal consistency, and the code claims above.

## Output
1. A rubric table: criterion → PASS/GAP → one-line evidence.
2. A ranked list of findings (most severe first): for each, the exact location/quote, why it's a problem, and a concrete fix. Separate "must-fix for DoD" from "nice-to-have".
3. Any factual discrepancy between the doc and the code, with the file:line evidence.
4. A final verdict: does the doc meet the DoD as-is, or what specifically blocks it.

---

# Independent Review: SFCC-123 Contentful Integration TSD

## 1. Rubric assessment

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence (one line) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Integration architecture & data flow, current-vs-target distinguished | **PASS** | §1 has target diagram + surface/token table, then a "Current implementation vs target (verified in code)" callout. Code confirms browser-side REST only; no SSR/GraphQL/webhook found anywhere in repo. |
| B | Content types for Sprint 1 AND Sprint 2, explicit, with existence status + backing story | **PASS** (minor consistency snag) | §2 prose gives an explicit S1 vs S2 split; table adds "Exists in code?" + backing story with Jira status. Snag: table's `Sprint` column uses ranges (`1-2`, `2-3`) that don't line up with the crisp prose split, and `2-3` implies an undefined Sprint 3. |
| C | SFCC-side consumption: APIs + fields + rendering logic, per surface | **PASS** | §3 "Already built" list + capability table (APIs/fields, rendering logic, status) per surface, all matching the tree. |
| D | Locale config aligned to storefronts, code-verified, earlier count discrepancy resolved | **PASS** (one unverifiable figure) | §4 table matches `sites.overlay.js` and `contentfulMapping.generated.ts` exactly (10 PWA sites, 9 locales, `en` default); count conflict explicitly resolved. The "EU site alone carries 5 locales" line is not code-verifiable (see finding 3). |
| E | Handoff boundary explicit and unambiguous | **PASS** | §5 table splits Accenture vs Contentful squad per concern. One row (composed pages) is openly "pending, see §6 item 7" rather than settled, but that is flagged as a blocker, not hidden. |
| F | Blockers & dependencies with owner + status | **PASS** | §6: 10 items, each with owner + status; hard blocker (item 8, credentials) surfaced in At-a-glance. |
| G | Briefing quality: at-a-glance, self-contained, lean, consistent, NO em/en dashes | **PASS** | "At a glance" section present; self-contained; zero em/en dashes confirmed by scan. Minor redundancy across §2/§5/§6/§8 (see finding 4). |
| H | Factual accuracy: no unverified claim as fact, no invented specifics | **PASS** (one minor imprecision) | All code specifics verified true. One imprecise accessor name (finding 1); the "5 EU locales" figure (finding 3) is attributed to a Confluence/BM source, so not a fabrication. |

**No criterion fails.** All findings below are polish, not DoD blockers.

## 2. Ranked findings

### Must-fix for DoD
None. The document satisfies every clause of the DoD and the six ticket tasks.

### Nice-to-have (ranked)

**1. Minor factual imprecision: `getConfig()` accessor name (§1, line 51).**
The doc says "Config comes from `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` via `getConfig()`." The runtime accessor the hooks actually call is **`getContentfulConfig()`** (`overrides/app/config/contentful.ts:19`; imported and called at `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:2,34`). `getConfig()` is the underlying PWA Kit `ssr-config` util that `contentful.ts` wraps internally (`contentful.ts:10,20`) — so the claim is defensible but reads as if the hook calls `getConfig()` directly.
*Fix:* change "via `getConfig()`" to "via `getContentfulConfig()`".

**2. Sprint column ranges conflict with the prose split (§2 table + §3 table).**
§2 prose is crisp: Sprint 1 = collection-hero, image-text, shoppable-image, homepage modules, promo announcement banner, global footer; Sprint 2 = PLP bottom-zone + inline grid insert + PDP size-guide; SEO FAQ = backlog. But the table's `Sprint` column shows `1-2`, `2-3`, etc. So the promo banner reads as "1-2" in the table yet "Sprint 1" in prose, and PLP types read "2-3" yet "Sprint 2" in prose. The `2-3` range also implies a Sprint 3 that is never defined. The doc already has a sentence explaining the value "is the range of the owning functional area," but the labels still read ambiguously against the prose.
*Fix:* set the table `Sprint` values to match the prose (`1` / `2` / `Backlog`), or drop the range column and rely on the prose split.

**3. "The EU site alone carries 5 locales" is not code-verifiable and superficially conflicts with the §4 table (§4, line 118).**
In the code layer, `ZimmermannEU` backs **4** single-locale PWA sites (`en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`) — see `config/sites.overlay.js:37-40` and `contentfulMapping.generated.ts:13-16`. The doc's own §4 table also shows only 4 EU-backed rows. The "5 locales" figure is attributed to Business Manager / SFCC-151 (a Confluence source, out of my verification scope), but a reader comparing it to the 4 rows shown will see a 4-vs-5 discrepancy.
*Fix:* name the 5th EU locale or add a half-sentence that it is a BM-level locale not surfaced in the PWA overlay, so the figure reconciles with the table.

**4. Mild redundancy across sections (§2, §5, §6, §8).**
The hotspots-representation reconciliation appears in the §2 note *and* §8 item 2; composed-page ownership appears in §5, §6 item 7, *and* §8 item 3. Acceptable cross-referencing for a briefing, but it inflates length slightly.
*Fix (optional):* state each once and cross-reference, e.g. "(open question 2)".

## 3. Factual discrepancies (doc vs code)

Only one, and it is minor:

| Doc claim | Code reality | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| §1: "Config comes from ... via `getConfig()`" | The runtime accessor is `getContentfulConfig()`; `getConfig()` is the PWA Kit util it wraps | `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts:19` (`export const getContentfulConfig`), `:10` + `:20` (imports/calls `getConfig` from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime`); `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:2,34` |

Everything else the doc asserts as code fact checks out exactly:
- `useContentful.ts` — two hooks, browser-side REST against `cdn.contentful.com`/`preview.contentful.com`, `include=2` (lines 43, 47, 106, 110). No SSR fetch, GraphQL, or webhook receiver anywhere in the repo (grep of `overrides`, `scripts` clean; only hits are a CSP allowlist and an unrelated pre-commit secret scanner).
- `contentfulMapping.ts` — `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` = only `shoppableImage` (line 54); `DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'en'` (line 24); tier env map `dev/test/sit/staging/uat/production→master` (lines 39-46).
- `definitions.ts` — exactly three Studio Experiences (`collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`) with the exact variable sets the doc lists.
- `hotspotPopup.tsx` — resolves `productId` via `useProduct` from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (line 3, 12) and renders the SFCC product image from `disBaseLink` (line 27), name, price, PDP link.
- `shoppableImage.tsx` — parses `hotspots` JSON into `{x, y, productId}` markers (lines 18-35, 59-61).
- `content-types/shoppableImage.js` — fields `title`/`image`/`imageAlt`/`hotspots` match §2 exactly (Symbol req / Asset link req / Symbol / Object).
- `sites.overlay.js` — the 10 PWA sites and 9 distinct locales (`en, en-US, en-GB, fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE`) match §4's table row-for-row; `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` in `contentfulMapping.generated.ts:8` is the same 9.
- All 15 internal link targets in §9 and inline `../` paths exist on disk. Both cited npm scripts (`sync:regional-config`, `generate:contentful`) exist in `package.json` (lines 72, 84). CSP allowlist includes `images.ctfassets.net`, `cdn.contentful.com`, `preview.contentful.com` as the doc states.

## 4. Verdict

**The document meets the Definition of Done as-is.** It is a self-contained briefing artefact covering integration architecture and data flow, the content model by sprint with existence status and backing stories, SFCC-side consumption per surface, locale configuration aligned to the storefronts and code-verified, an explicit Accenture-vs-Contentful-squad handoff boundary, and a blockers list with owners and statuses. Current-vs-target is honestly distinguished, and the earlier locale-count conflict is resolved. No em/en dashes.

Nothing blocks sign-off. The four nice-to-have items are polish: correct `getConfig()` → `getContentfulConfig()` (finding 1), reconcile the Sprint-column ranges with the prose split (finding 2), and clarify or reconcile the "5 EU locales" figure (finding 3). I would not hold publication for any of them, though finding 1 is a quick, worthwhile correction since the briefing is going to an external squad.

# Independent Review: SFCC-123 Contentful Integration TSD

## 1. Rubric assessment

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence (one line) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Integration architecture & data flow, current-vs-target distinguished | **PASS** | §1 has target diagram + surface/token table, then a "Current implementation vs target (verified in code)" callout. Code confirms browser-side REST only; no SSR/GraphQL/webhook found anywhere in repo. |
| B | Content types for Sprint 1 AND Sprint 2, explicit, with existence status + backing story | **PASS** (minor consistency snag) | §2 prose gives an explicit S1 vs S2 split; table adds "Exists in code?" + backing story with Jira status. Snag: table's `Sprint` column uses ranges (`1-2`, `2-3`) that don't line up with the crisp prose split, and `2-3` implies an undefined Sprint 3. |
| C | SFCC-side consumption: APIs + fields + rendering logic, per surface | **PASS** | §3 "Already built" list + capability table (APIs/fields, rendering logic, status) per surface, all matching the tree. |
| D | Locale config aligned to storefronts, code-verified, earlier count discrepancy resolved | **PASS** (one unverifiable figure) | §4 table matches `sites.overlay.js` and `contentfulMapping.generated.ts` exactly (10 PWA sites, 9 locales, `en` default); count conflict explicitly resolved. The "EU site alone carries 5 locales" line is not code-verifiable (see finding 3). |
| E | Handoff boundary explicit and unambiguous | **PASS** | §5 table splits Accenture vs Contentful squad per concern. One row (composed pages) is openly "pending, see §6 item 7" rather than settled, but that is flagged as a blocker, not hidden. |
| F | Blockers & dependencies with owner + status | **PASS** | §6: 10 items, each with owner + status; hard blocker (item 8, credentials) surfaced in At-a-glance. |
| G | Briefing quality: at-a-glance, self-contained, lean, consistent, NO em/en dashes | **PASS** | "At a glance" section present; self-contained; zero em/en dashes confirmed by scan. Minor redundancy across §2/§5/§6/§8 (see finding 4). |
| H | Factual accuracy: no unverified claim as fact, no invented specifics | **PASS** (one minor imprecision) | All code specifics verified true. One imprecise accessor name (finding 1); the "5 EU locales" figure (finding 3) is attributed to a Confluence/BM source, so not a fabrication. |

**No criterion fails.** All findings below are polish, not DoD blockers.

## 2. Ranked findings

### Must-fix for DoD
None. The document satisfies every clause of the DoD and the six ticket tasks.

### Nice-to-have (ranked)

**1. Minor factual imprecision: `getConfig()` accessor name (§1, line 51).**
The doc says "Config comes from `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` via `getConfig()`." The runtime accessor the hooks actually call is **`getContentfulConfig()`** (`overrides/app/config/contentful.ts:19`; imported and called at `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:2,34`). `getConfig()` is the underlying PWA Kit `ssr-config` util that `contentful.ts` wraps internally (`contentful.ts:10,20`) — so the claim is defensible but reads as if the hook calls `getConfig()` directly.
*Fix:* change "via `getConfig()`" to "via `getContentfulConfig()`".

**2. Sprint column ranges conflict with the prose split (§2 table + §3 table).**
§2 prose is crisp: Sprint 1 = collection-hero, image-text, shoppable-image, homepage modules, promo announcement banner, global footer; Sprint 2 = PLP bottom-zone + inline grid insert + PDP size-guide; SEO FAQ = backlog. But the table's `Sprint` column shows `1-2`, `2-3`, etc. So the promo banner reads as "1-2" in the table yet "Sprint 1" in prose, and PLP types read "2-3" yet "Sprint 2" in prose. The `2-3` range also implies a Sprint 3 that is never defined. The doc already has a sentence explaining the value "is the range of the owning functional area," but the labels still read ambiguously against the prose.
*Fix:* set the table `Sprint` values to match the prose (`1` / `2` / `Backlog`), or drop the range column and rely on the prose split.

**3. "The EU site alone carries 5 locales" is not code-verifiable and superficially conflicts with the §4 table (§4, line 118).**
In the code layer, `ZimmermannEU` backs **4** single-locale PWA sites (`en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`) — see `config/sites.overlay.js:37-40` and `contentfulMapping.generated.ts:13-16`. The doc's own §4 table also shows only 4 EU-backed rows. The "5 locales" figure is attributed to Business Manager / SFCC-151 (a Confluence source, out of my verification scope), but a reader comparing it to the 4 rows shown will see a 4-vs-5 discrepancy.
*Fix:* name the 5th EU locale or add a half-sentence that it is a BM-level locale not surfaced in the PWA overlay, so the figure reconciles with the table.

**4. Mild redundancy across sections (§2, §5, §6, §8).**
The hotspots-representation reconciliation appears in the §2 note *and* §8 item 2; composed-page ownership appears in §5, §6 item 7, *and* §8 item 3. Acceptable cross-referencing for a briefing, but it inflates length slightly.
*Fix (optional):* state each once and cross-reference, e.g. "(open question 2)".

## 3. Factual discrepancies (doc vs code)

Only one, and it is minor:

| Doc claim | Code reality | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| §1: "Config comes from ... via `getConfig()`" | The runtime accessor is `getContentfulConfig()`; `getConfig()` is the PWA Kit util it wraps | `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts:19` (`export const getContentfulConfig`), `:10` + `:20` (imports/calls `getConfig` from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime`); `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:2,34` |

Everything else the doc asserts as code fact checks out exactly:
- `useContentful.ts` — two hooks, browser-side REST against `cdn.contentful.com`/`preview.contentful.com`, `include=2` (lines 43, 47, 106, 110). No SSR fetch, GraphQL, or webhook receiver anywhere in the repo (grep of `overrides`, `scripts` clean; only hits are a CSP allowlist and an unrelated pre-commit secret scanner).
- `contentfulMapping.ts` — `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` = only `shoppableImage` (line 54); `DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'en'` (line 24); tier env map `dev/test/sit/staging/uat/production→master` (lines 39-46).
- `definitions.ts` — exactly three Studio Experiences (`collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`) with the exact variable sets the doc lists.
- `hotspotPopup.tsx` — resolves `productId` via `useProduct` from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (line 3, 12) and renders the SFCC product image from `disBaseLink` (line 27), name, price, PDP link.
- `shoppableImage.tsx` — parses `hotspots` JSON into `{x, y, productId}` markers (lines 18-35, 59-61).
- `content-types/shoppableImage.js` — fields `title`/`image`/`imageAlt`/`hotspots` match §2 exactly (Symbol req / Asset link req / Symbol / Object).
- `sites.overlay.js` — the 10 PWA sites and 9 distinct locales (`en, en-US, en-GB, fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE`) match §4's table row-for-row; `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` in `contentfulMapping.generated.ts:8` is the same 9.
- All 15 internal link targets in §9 and inline `../` paths exist on disk. Both cited npm scripts (`sync:regional-config`, `generate:contentful`) exist in `package.json` (lines 72, 84). CSP allowlist includes `images.ctfassets.net`, `cdn.contentful.com`, `preview.contentful.com` as the doc states.

## 4. Verdict

**The document meets the Definition of Done as-is.** It is a self-contained briefing artefact covering integration architecture and data flow, the content model by sprint with existence status and backing stories, SFCC-side consumption per surface, locale configuration aligned to the storefronts and code-verified, an explicit Accenture-vs-Contentful-squad handoff boundary, and a blockers list with owners and statuses. Current-vs-target is honestly distinguished, and the earlier locale-count conflict is resolved. No em/en dashes.

Nothing blocks sign-off. The four nice-to-have items are polish: correct `getConfig()` → `getContentfulConfig()` (finding 1), reconcile the Sprint-column ranges with the prose split (finding 2), and clarify or reconcile the "5 EU locales" figure (finding 3). I would not hold publication for any of them, though finding 1 is a quick, worthwhile correction since the briefing is going to an external squad.

1	# TSD: Contentful Integration, SFCC-Side Design & Content Model (SFCC-123)
2	
3	> **Status:** 🟡 In progress · **Owner:** Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz · **Reporter:** Jasmijn Tsang · **Epic:** [SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-1) · **Updated:** 2026-07-22
