# Contentful Integration Technical Design & Content Model (SFCC-123)

## Overview

Editorial and CMS content in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team. MRT (Managed Runtime, Salesforce's PWA hosting layer) acts as the integration layer between Contentful and the browser-rendered PWA storefront.

| Direction | Flow |
| --- | --- |
| Inbound (Contentful to MRT) | Published content entries (hero banners, editorial modules, navigation, footer, announcement banners, size guides, accordion copy) delivered via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA) to the MRT SSR layer on every page render. |
| Outbound (MRT to Contentful) | Cache-purge webhook acknowledgements; Management API calls from CI for schema migrations. No content flows from SFCC back to Contentful. |
| NOT in this flow | SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly. All CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. |

Contentful is the sole CMS for all eight Zimmermann storefronts. SFCC manages commerce data (products, pricing, orders); Contentful manages editorial data (copy, imagery configuration, page layouts). They complement each other without overlap.

## Integration Architecture & Data Flow

Pattern: Contentful to MRT (Node/SSR) to browser, SSR-first for SEO/LCP.

Architecture diagram: PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration) with CDA (published content, SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on post-hydration reads; public token safe in bundle), CPA (draft content, editor preview only, token server-side in MRT, proxied through an MRT preview endpoint), Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net, srcset/sizes/avif|webp), and Publish webhook to MRT /webhooks/contentful (clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish, HMAC-verified).

### API surface & token boundary

| Surface | Origin / Boundary | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN (public, read-only) | SSR-first; browser hydrates from SSR payload. Safe to embed in bundle. |
| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN (server-side) | Editor preview via iframe postMessage. Never reaches browser. |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI host only | CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN | Never in MRT/bundle, build-time only. Never embedded, never in PR diffs. |
| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish. TTL fallback 60s SWR. Rejected and logged if HMAC fails. |

Key behaviours confirmed in 02-contentful.md:
- SSR first. Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload, no CDA call on first paint.
- GraphQL for composed pages. Where a page assembles many entries, the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
- Live preview. When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on postMessage events from Studio.
- Asset delivery. Images come from images.ctfassets.net. The storefront generates srcset, sizes, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint. images.ctfassets.net is preconnected from the document head.
- SSR cache TTL. 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache, the TTL is the fallback if a webhook drops.
- CDN rate limit. 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic, risk only during burst republish events.
- Bundle weight. Rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
- No PII flows through Contentful.

### Content Ownership (from 02-contentful.md)

SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001).

| Surface | SFCC Owns | Contentful Owns | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules, hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
| Size guides | - | Fallback content only. Primary size guide is Measmerize overlay (PRD-053). | Confirmed |
| Footer | - | All content | Confirmed |
| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM, SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | Pending |
| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary is Measmerize, PRD-053) | Pending |
| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | Pending |
| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy, managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005) | - | Confirmed |

## Content Model Requirements

### SPRINT 1 Content Types, Required Now

Derived from active and blocked Jira stories. Each type requires a TypeScript React component in overrides/ and a schema definition in scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js.

| Content Type | Required By | Key Fields | Locale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Promotional Announcement Banner | SFCC-51 (Blocked), SFCC-111 | messages[], CTA link, rotation timing, page visibility, position, per-customer-group config, scheduling (start/end), enabled flag | Yes, per storefront |
| Global Footer | SFCC-55, SFCC-117 | nav link columns, legal/copyright text, region-specific links (e.g. AU Acknowledgement of Country), bottom bar | Yes, per storefront |
| Homepage Hero Banner | SFCC-90, SFCC-58 | image, headline, subheadline, CTA link, full-bleed vs padded variant | Yes |
| Homepage Content Row / Image Grid | SFCC-94 | images[], column count (2/3/4), CTA link per image, carousel flag | Yes |
| Homepage Editorial Feature Block | SFCC-90 | editorial image, title, body copy, CTA link, optional product tile link | Yes |
| Navigation / Mega Menu | SFCC-96, SFCC-52 | top-level nav items[], subcategory links[], editorial image slot (optional), per-storefront cloneable | Yes, per storefront |

### SPRINT 2 Content Types

| Content Type | Required By | Key Fields | Locale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Size Guide | SFCC-102 | size guide content per product type, images/table data | Yes |
| PLP Bottom Zone Editorial Slots | SFCC-82 | full-width image block, editorial feature block, two-column content block, each with image, title, copy, CTA | Yes |
| PLP Inline Grid Insert | SFCC-190 | campaign image, editorial text (optional), featured product tile (optional), position, per-category config | Yes |
| PDP Accordion Content | SFCC-195 | accordion tab label, body copy (rich text), per-storefront, Shipping & Returns, Assistance tabs | Yes, per storefront |
| Checkout Trust Messaging | SFCC-67 | trust message blocks, Collect in Boutique disclaimer, delivery disclaimer | Yes, per storefront |
| Returns / Refund Messaging | SFCC-14 | configurable refund processing note | Yes, per storefront |

### Identified, Sprint TBD

| Content Type | Jira | Target Sprint | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Z.immerse editorial page templates | SFCC-10 | Sprint 5 | Full flexible component library. Content model needs design before build. |
| Mini-cart Shop the Look | SFCC-11 | TBD | Editorial content slot inside mini-cart. |
| FAQ / Article structured data | SFCC-173 | TBD | JSON-LD schema enrichment for GEO/AI Overviews. |
| Homepage personalisation (authenticated) | SFCC-160 | Year 2 | Full Contentful personalisation, pending contract timeline. |
| Countdown timer module | SFCC-162 | TBD | Could Have, pending design confirmation. |

### What is NOT in Contentful

Do not model these in Contentful, owned by other systems:
- Product data (names, descriptions, pricing, stock), AP21 to MuleSoft to SFCC
- Product imagery, SFCC Business Manager static content library
- Orders, customer data, basket, SFCC / NewStore / Omneo
- Tax rules, pricebooks, checkout configuration, SFCC Business Manager
- GTM tags, analytics configuration, Tell No Lies

## SFCC-Side Consumption & Build Scope

Already built:
- Config/types: overrides/app/config/contentful.ts, config/contentfulMapping.ts, types/contentful.ts
- Data hook: overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts
- Components: components/contentful/{heroBanner, productHero, duplexSection, videoEmbed}.tsx
- Studio Experiences: components/contentful/experiences/{shoppableImage.tsx, definitions.ts}, pages/experience/index.tsx
- Schema-as-code + tooling: scripts/contentful/{sync.js, generateDefinitions.mjs, migrations/, setup/bootstrapSpace.mjs}
- Runtime: CSP allowances in overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts, Studio registration via .claude/skills/contentful-register-component

| Capability | APIs / Fields Consumed | Rendering Logic | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Promotional Announcement Banner | CDA: messages[], ctaLink, rotationInterval, enabled, scheduledStart/End, position, customerGroup, enabledPages | Rotate client-side. Suppress if enabled=false or outside schedule. Match customerGroup vs SFCC session. | To build, SFCC-51 blocked |
| Homepage Hero Banner | CDA: image (Asset), headline, subheadline, ctaText, ctaLink, variant (full-bleed/padded) | SSR as h1. Image via Contentful Images API w=1920&fm=webp. Omit CTA if null. | To build, SFCC-90 |
| Homepage Content Row / Image Grid | CDA: images[] (Assets), columnCount (2/3/4), ctaLink per image, carouselFlag | Grid or carousel by columnCount. All images via Contentful Images API. | To build, SFCC-94 |
| Homepage Editorial Feature Block | CDA: image, title, bodyCopy, ctaLink, productTileLink (optional) | SSR render. Omit product tile if null. | To build, SFCC-90 |
| Navigation / Mega Menu | CDA: navItems[] (label, link, hasMegaMenu, subcategories[], editorialImage, editorialLink) | Preserve Contentful item order. No dropdown if hasMegaMenu=false. | To build, SFCC-96 |
| Global Footer | CDA: navLinkColumns[], legalText, regionLinks[], bottomBar | SSR. Region-specific links filtered by SFCC site ID. | To build, SFCC-55 |
| PLP Bottom Zone Editorial Slots | CDA: fullWidthImageBlock, editorialFeatureBlock, twoColumnContentBlock | Render below PLP grid. Locale-aware. | To build, SFCC-82 |
| PLP Inline Grid Insert | CDA: campaignImage, editorialText (optional), featuredProductTile (optional), position, categoryConfig | Inject into grid at configured position. Show only when matched by current category. | To build, SFCC-190 |
| PDP Size Guide Fallback | CDA: sizeGuideContent per product type, images/table data | Show only when Measmerize returns no data for the product (PRD-053). | To build, SFCC-102 |
| PDP Accordion Content | CDA: accordionLabel, bodyCopy (rich text), per storefront | Render as accordion tabs (Shipping & Returns, Assistance). Rich text via Contentful rich-text renderer. | To build, SFCC-195 |
| Checkout Trust Messaging | CDA: trustMessageBlocks[], collectInBoutiqueDisclaimer, deliveryDisclaimer, per storefront | Render in checkout flow. | To build, SFCC-67 |
| Returns / Refund Messaging | CDA: refundNote, per storefront | Render in My Account refund status view. | To build, SFCC-14 |

### Error Handling & Monitoring

| Scenario | Handling |
| --- | --- |
| Contentful CDA unavailable during SSR | Render the page without editorial content. Log the error. Commerce data (SFCC) is unaffected. NEVER block the page render on CMS availability. |
| Contentful entry field is null or missing | Component must handle gracefully with a null-safe default. No uncaught exceptions from missing CMS data. |
| Invalid HMAC on incoming webhook | Return 401 immediately. Do not process. Log the attempt. |
| Schema drift detected in CI gate | CI exits non-zero. Deploy is blocked. Developer must run npm run migrate:contentful before re-triggering. |
| Migration script fails mid-run | Contentful does not roll back automatically. Developer must assess partial state and write a compensating migration. |
| Preview API accessed from browser | Should be architecturally impossible, CPA is MRT server-side only. If a browser request reaches CPA, treat as a security incident. |
| Consent gating failure (Didomi) | Fail closed: no third-party scripts load. Affects Vimeo embeds in editorial content. See SFCC-106. |

Graceful degradation is non-negotiable: Contentful being unavailable must never break the commerce experience.

## Environment & Locale Configuration

Detailed reference: Contentful CMS, Setup & Operations.

### Six-Tier Delivery Pipeline

One Contentful Space, one Environment per delivery tier. Promotion is always sequential.

| Tier | Name | Contentful Env ID | MRT Push Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 & 2 | DEV | dev | npm run push:dev | Feature development and integration testing |
| 3 | TEST | test | npm run push:test | Digital QA (being created) |
| 4 | OMS INT (SIT) | sit | npm run push:sit | NewStore SIT regression |
| 5 | STAGE | staging | npm run push:staging | Full E2E with live third parties |
| 6 | UAT | uat | npm run push:uat | Business acceptance across all regions |
| 7 | PRODUCTION | master (via production alias) | npm run push:prod | Live customer-facing production |

### Production Alias Strategy, Zero-Downtime Releases

Production MRT uses CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production, which resolves to a Contentful alias. Flipping the alias is how zero-downtime releases are performed. Steps: clone production env for the release; run migrations against the clone (npm run migrate:contentful -- --target release-YYYY-MM); test directly against the release env; promote by flipping production and master aliases atomically (npm run promote:alias -- --target release-YYYY-MM); keep previous env 14 days as rollback then delete. The production alias requires the Contentful Enterprise plan.

### The Nine Contentful Locales

These locale codes match config/sites.js in the PWA repo exactly. No runtime mapping required.

| Locale Code | Name | Storefront(s) | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| en | English (AU) | ZimmermannAU | Default |
| en-US | English (US) | ZimmermannUS | en |
| en-GB | English (UK / EU) | ZimmermannUK, ZimmermannEUen | en |
| fr | French | ZimmermannEUfr | en |
| it | Italian | ZimmermannEUit | en |
| es | Spanish | ZimmermannEUes | en |
| en-CH | English (EU International) | ZimmermannEUIntl | en |
| en-HK | English (HK) | ZimmermannHK | en |
| en-AE | English (ME) | ZimmermannME | en |

### Locale Rules for Content Modellers

- Translatable fields (headline, body copy, CTA text, alt text) to set localized: true.
- Structural fields (asset links, layout flags, product IDs) to set localized: false, shared across all locales.
- Fallback chain: if a locale (e.g. fr) has no content for a field, Contentful falls back to en automatically.
- Translation pipeline: Transperfect is the translation partner (HPC-006). Strategy under discussion, Contentful squad to own.

## SFCC / PWA Touchpoints

- API token boundary: CDA read-only browser-safe; CPA server-only via MRT proxy; CMA local/CI only, never deployed to MRT; webhook secret MRT env var only.
- MRT environment variables must be set per tier. Use Contentful CMS, Setup & Operations as the setup reference.
- PWA component requirements: typed React component in overrides/ for each content type; handle null CMS fields safely; register visual-editor components in Studio Experiences and cover entry-to-props transforms with Vitest.
- Content Type to Component field mappings maintained in scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js and component props/types.

## Handoff Boundary, Accenture vs Contentful Squad

| Concern | Accenture (SFCC-side) Builds | Incoming Contentful Squad Owns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Integration | MRT connection, CDA/CPA/webhook wiring, SSR cache, CSP | - |
| Content types | Schema-as-code definitions + typed React components | Content authoring, Studio operations, extending model beyond Sprint 1 & 2 |
| Environments / locales | Consume per-tier env vars | Space setup, environment/alias/locale bootstrap |
| Content ownership | Commerce data (product/price/inventory) | All editorial (banners, modules, lookbooks, footer, navigation) |
| Translations | - | Transperfect integration, translation memory, workflow (HPC-006) |
| Studio Experiences | Register components in experiences module | Operate Studio visual editor; create/configure page layouts |
| Composed pages (PDP/PLP editorial split) | Pending | Pending |

### Developer Setup Reference (steps)

1. Clone + install (also installs Husky Git hooks): git clone + npm ci
2. Copy env template: cp .env.sample .env
3. Fill CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN + CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID (ask Integration Lead or npm run config:contentful)
4. Generate personal CMA token: app.contentful.com to avatar to Account Settings to CMA Tokens; save as CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN in .env
5. Start local dev server: npm start (fetches from Contentful dev env live)

Never commit .env. Pre-commit hook blocks commits containing secret-shaped values.

### One-Time Space Bootstrap Status

| Bootstrap Step | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Generate CI service account CMA token + store as CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN in GitHub Actions | Complete |
| Bootstrap environments, locales, API keys, production alias (npm run setup:contentful) | Complete |
| Create MRT TEST environment | Complete |
| Install Contentful Studio app in the space | Complete |
| Set MRT environment variables per tier (CONTENTFUL_* + CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET) | Incomplete, 4 of 9 items remaining |
| Configure Contentful to MRT cache-purge webhook per environment | Incomplete |
| Restrict content type editing in sit/staging/uat/master to CI service account | Incomplete |
| Add CI service account CMA token as GitHub Actions secret | Incomplete |

## Blockers & Dependencies Before Squad Onboards

| # | Blocker / Dependency | Owner | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Locale count: confirm the canonical 11-locale set against config/sites.js before locale bootstrap. 02-contentful.md says 11; Confluence ops page says 9. | Zimmermann | Open |
| 2 | MRT env vars per tier not set (CONTENTFUL_* + CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET), ops checklist item 4 | Tier-1 approver / Accenture | Incomplete |
| 3 | Contentful to MRT cache-purge webhook not configured, ops checklist item 5 | Accenture | Incomplete |
| 4 | Content-type editing not yet restricted to CI service account in sit/staging/uat/master, ops item 8 | Accenture | Incomplete |
| 5 | CI service-account CMA token not added as GH Actions secret, ops item 9 | Accenture | Incomplete |
| 6 | regions content-model field unconfirmed (02-contentful.md), affects cross-storefront authoring | Content strategy | Open |
| 7 | Composed-page ownership unconfirmed: PDP/PLP editorial and mega-menu tiles, 02-contentful.md | Tim / Content | Open |
| 8 | Per-environment Contentful credentials to be provided to incoming squad (Space ID, CDA/CPA tokens, webhook secret), 02-contentful.md | Contentful squad | Open |
| 9 | Didomi purpose IDs for consent-gated components (e.g. Vimeo embeds in editorial). Blocked pending Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley review. | Zimmermann | Blocked |
| 10 | Contentful Enterprise plan, required for production alias (zero-downtime releases). Confirm with Zimmermann. | Zimmermann | Confirm |

## Key Design Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single Contentful Space for all 8 storefronts | One Space, per-locale content fields | Locale model handles per-storefront variation. Avoids content duplication. |
| Schema as code, not hand-created in UI | Git-managed definitions deployed via npm run sync:contentful | Prevents schema drift, enables code review, gives CI visibility. |
| CDA token in browser bundle (delivery only) | Delivery API token is browser-safe | CDA tokens are read-only and scoped to one environment. |
| Production alias instead of fixed environment name | CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production resolves to an alias | Enables zero-downtime releases. Requires Contentful Enterprise plan. |
| ISR cache invalidation via webhook on publish | Contentful fires HMAC-signed webhook to MRT invalidates cache | Without cache invalidation, published content changes would not appear until TTL expires. |
| Graceful degradation for CMS unavailability | Render page without editorial content if Contentful is down | Commerce functionality must never be blocked by CMS availability. |
| Contentful SDK v11, no connection pool isolation hook | Mitigate via graceful degradation | SDK v11 does not expose a dispatcher hook for custom connection pooling. |

Ownership boundary table: Contentful space provisioning & billing (Zimmermann); content type definitions/schema-as-code (Accenture Squad-A initial + Contentful Squad expands); content authoring (Contentful Squad/Zimmermann); translation Transperfect (Contentful Squad); PWA components rendering Contentful (Accenture Squad-A); Contentful SDK integration (Accenture, contentful v11, SSR fetching, ISR cache invalidation, graceful degradation); cache-purge webhook receiver in MRT (Accenture Squad-A); Studio Experiences (Accenture sets up, Contentful squad operates); environment provisioning (Accenture initial, Contentful squad ongoing); CI/CD Contentful pipeline (Accenture); Contentful Roles (Accenture initial setup).

### Accenture Build Checklist

Infrastructure & Auth: create CI service account + CMA token in GitHub Actions; run npm run setup:contentful; set all MRT env vars per tier; configure Contentful roles.
PWA Integration: integrate Contentful SDK (contentful v11), SSR fetching via CDA; implement Preview API proxy (MRT server-side); implement HMAC-verified cache-purge webhook receiver in MRT Node layer; implement graceful degradation.

| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish. TTL fallback 60s SWR. Rejected and logged if HMAC fails. |

Key behaviours confirmed in 02-contentful.md:
- SSR first. Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload, no CDA call on first paint.
- GraphQL for composed pages. Where a page assembles many entries, the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
- Live preview. When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on postMessage events from Studio.
- Asset delivery. Images come from images.ctfassets.net. The storefront generates srcset, sizes, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint. images.ctfassets.net is preconnected from the document head.
- SSR cache TTL. 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache, the TTL is the fallback if a webhook drops.
- CDN rate limit. 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic, risk only during burst republish events.
- Bundle weight. Rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
- No PII flows through Contentful.

### Error Handling & Monitoring

| Scenario | Handling |
| --- | --- |
| Contentful CDA unavailable during SSR | Render the page without editorial content. Log the error. Commerce data (SFCC) is unaffected. NEVER block the page render on CMS availability. |
| Contentful entry field is null or missing | Component must handle gracefully with a null-safe default. No uncaught exceptions from missing CMS data. |
| Invalid HMAC on incoming webhook | Return 401 immediately. Do not process. Log the attempt. |
| Schema drift detected in CI gate | CI exits non-zero. Deploy is blocked. Developer must run npm run migrate:contentful before re-triggering. |
| Migration script fails mid-run | Contentful does not roll back automatically. Developer must assess partial state and write a compensating migration. |
| Preview API accessed from browser | Should be architecturally impossible, CPA is MRT server-side only. If a browser request reaches CPA, treat as a security incident. |
| Consent gating failure (Didomi) | Fail closed: no third-party scripts load. Affects Vimeo embeds in editorial content. See SFCC-106. |

Graceful degradation is non-negotiable: Contentful being unavailable must never break the commerce experience.

## Environment & Locale Configuration

### Six-Tier Delivery Pipeline

One Contentful Space, one Environment per delivery tier. Promotion is always sequential.

| Tier | Name | Contentful Env ID | MRT Push Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 & 2 | DEV | dev | npm run push:dev | Feature development and integration testing |

| 7 | PRODUCTION | master (via production alias) | npm run push:prod | Live customer-facing production |

### Production Alias Strategy, Zero-Downtime Releases

Production MRT uses CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production, which resolves to a Contentful alias. Flipping the alias is how zero-downtime releases are performed. Steps: clone production env for the release; run migrations against the clone (npm run migrate:contentful -- --target release-YYYY-MM); test directly against the release env; promote by flipping production and master aliases atomically (npm run promote:alias -- --target release-YYYY-MM); keep previous env 14 days as rollback then delete. The production alias requires the Contentful Enterprise plan.

## Key Design Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single Contentful Space for all 8 storefronts | One Space, per-locale content fields | Locale model handles per-storefront variation. Avoids content duplication. |
| Schema as code, not hand-created in UI | Git-managed definitions deployed via npm run sync:contentful | Prevents schema drift, enables code review, gives CI visibility. |
| CDA token in browser bundle (delivery only) | Delivery API token is browser-safe | CDA tokens are read-only and scoped to one environment. |
| Production alias instead of fixed environment name | CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production resolves to an alias | Enables zero-downtime releases. Requires Contentful Enterprise plan. |
| ISR cache invalidation via webhook on publish | Contentful fires HMAC-signed webhook to MRT invalidates cache | Without cache invalidation, published content changes would not appear until TTL expires. |
| Graceful degradation for CMS unavailability | Render page without editorial content if Contentful is down | Commerce functionality must never be blocked by CMS availability. |
| Contentful SDK v11, no connection pool isolation hook | Mitigate via graceful degradation | SDK v11 does not expose a dispatcher hook for custom connection pooling. |

Parent epic **SFCC-1** (Platform Setup & Environments). **Assignee: Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz**; reporter Jasmijn Tsang. Created 2026-07-08. Sibling spikes: SFCC-121/122 (see [[sfcc-122]]). Board house style Objective/Background/Tasks/DoD (see [[f2r-spike]]).

Objective: document the Contentful→MRT→SFCC integration + data flow, define Sprint 1/2 content types, define what SFCC consumes (APIs, fields, rendering), locale config across the storefronts, and the Accenture-vs-incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary. DoD: a TSD briefing artefact for the incoming Contentful squad.

An independent reviewer subagent confirmed all DoD criteria pass and spot-checked every code claim true. A second confirmatory pass validated the Confluence/Jira claims directly: fixed a wrong section citation (imagery claim is PWA TSD §9 Performance Strategy, not §11) and refined the credentials blocker (owner "Zimmermann IT / Contentful"; add environment ID); all 11 Jira story statuses re-confirmed unchanged; credentials hard-blocker (page 268337165) confirmed verbatim. Published as DRAFT 2026-07-22 to SFCC space under "05.1 - Architecture & Solution Design" (parent 277577731, sibling of the SFCC-122 draft): page id **351207428**, title "[DRAFT] TSD: Contentful Integration - SFCC-Side Design & Content Model (Spike SFCC-123)", label `draft`, top-of-page draft banner, URL https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/351207428. Repo-relative links were stripped to plain code spans for the Confluence version (absolute Jira/Confluence links kept). Still NOT linked on the SFCC-123 ticket and NOT announced to the squad (draft-only, same pattern as [[sfcc-122]]). To finalise: remove banner + `[DRAFT]` title prefix + `draft` label, fold in squad review, then link on the ticket. Sibling deliverable SFCC-122 lives at `zimmermann-pwa/.docs/spikes/SFCC-122-mrt-api-capabilities.md`.

**Crux/reframe (same shape as [[sfcc-122]]):** the SFCC-side Contentful integration is already substantially BUILT & documented, not greenfield discovery. Codebase `zimmermann-pwa`: `scripts/contentful/` (sync.js, migrations/, setup/ bootstrapSpace+getConfig+runMigrations+promoteAlias+detectDrift, generateDefinitions.mjs), `overrides/app/components/contentful/` (heroBanner, duplexSection, productHero, videoEmbed) + `experiences/` (collectionHero, imageText, shoppableImage, hotspotPopup/Marker), `hooks/useContentful.ts`, config/contentful.ts + contentfulMapping(.generated).ts, types/contentful.ts, `.claude/skills/contentful-register-component`, CI contentful-drift-audit + Husky pre-commit drift check. Deps: contentful, contentful-management, contentful-cli, @contentful/experiences-sdk-react, @contentful/live-preview. Integration doc: `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` (CDA/CPA/CMA split, publish webhook→MRT cache purge, SSR-first+GraphQL, Images API, failure modes). Architecture: single Contentful Space, one env per delivery tier.

Key findings (verified 2026-07-22): (a) **Locale RESOLVED** — not a data conflict, a category error: 8 SFCC sites/storefront catalogues (EU carries 5 locales), 10 PWA sites (EU domestic split into en/fr/it/es single-locale PWA sites), 9 distinct Contentful locales (`en` default, en-US, en-GB, fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE) per `config/sites.overlay.js` + `contentfulMapping.ts`. `02-contentful.md §7`'s "Eleven" is WRONG (wrongly includes `en-AU` = BM site default the AU PWA overrides to `en`, plus a separate `en (EU)`); fix §7 to 9 — pending. (b) Content model immature: only `shoppableImage` CDA content type codified + 3 Studio Experiences (collection-hero/image-text/shoppable-image); editorial components heroBanner/duplexSection/videoEmbed/productHero exist without a confirmed content type. (c) **Current code vs documented target diverges:** live data layer `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` is a BROWSER-SIDE REST fetch (CDA/CPA, include=2); the SSR-first fetch, GraphQL Content API, and publish-webhook receiver described in `02-contentful.md §3`/PWA TSD §7 are NOT yet built. (d) **NEW discrepancy:** product image ownership contradicts across Confluence — PWA TSD (256835585) §11 says ALL imagery incl. product served from Contentful (images.ctfassets.net; DMU-010/CRM-075/HPC-003), but Product TSD (292061208) §4.3/§9 say product images load directly into SFCC, no external DAM. (e) Ownership (`02-contentful.md §1`) marks PLP/PDP editorial split, mega-menu promo tiles, category-landing routing *pending*. (f) Human setup checklist incomplete: MRT env vars per tier, Contentful→MRT cache-purge webhook, Contentful roles, CI CMA GitHub secret. (g) **Hard blocker** (Confluence 268337165): Contentful must provide per-env credentials (Space ID, CDA/CPA tokens, webhook secret). Contentful integration is NOT a separate sprint — it rides each functional story (`.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`). Mapped Contentful stories: SFCC-51 (promo banner, Blocked), 55 (footer), 82/203 (PLP bottom zone), 90 (homepage modules), 102 (PDP size-guide fallback, non-Measmerize), 151 (locale/URL config, 8 storefronts), 173 (SEO FAQ/Article JSON-LD), 190/204 (PLP inline grid insert).

Key Confluence (space SFCC): 318472193 "Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations" (v7, ops runbook: 6-tier env topology, alias/release workflow, token matrix, locales, content types, drift, scripts, checklist), 292061208 (TSD Product), 303890433 (Third Party Integrations — App Exchange connector + Delivery API), 257327107 (PDP editorial blocks), 303104002 (Regional Storefronts/locales), 268337165 (Third Party Credentials — blocker), 258408463 (Decision Log — images Contentful vs SFCC), 303071234 (Homepage & Content model/authoring), 257163278 (Product — content-type open questions).

content.content:
1	> **DRAFT: Spike SFCC-123.** Working briefing for the incoming Contentful squad, fact-checked against the codebase, Confluence, and Jira as of 22 Jul 2026. Not yet ratified by the squad; open items and the handoff boundary are not final.
2	
3	# TSD: Contentful Integration, SFCC-Side Design & Content Model (SFCC-123)
4	
5	> **Status:** In progress · **Owner:** Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz · **Reporter:** Jasmijn Tsang · **Epic:** [SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-1) · **Updated:** 2026-07-22
6	> **Audience:** the incoming Contentful squad (briefing artefact) plus Squad A engineers building the SFCC-side connection.
7	> **Provenance:** seeded from the SFCC-123 template and fact-checked against the codebase, Confluence, and the linked Jira stories on 2026-07-22. Items still unconfirmed are called out as open, never asserted as fact.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## At a glance
12	
13	- **What this is:** the SFCC-side briefing for the incoming Contentful squad, covering integration architecture, the content model SFCC must consume, locale setup, and build scope. It is the work tracked as Open Item #3 on the Product TSD.
14	- **State of play:** the integration is substantially scaffolded (config, data hooks, Studio Experiences, schema-as-code tooling, CSP, CI drift checks), but the SSR-first fetch, the GraphQL Content API, the publish-webhook receiver, and most editorial content types are still to build.
15	- **Content model today:** one CDA content type (`shoppableImage`) plus three Studio Experiences (`collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`). Everything else in §2 is to build.
16	- **Locale:** 8 SFCC sites, 10 PWA sites, 9 Contentful locales (`en` default). The earlier count conflict is resolved (§4).
17	- **Hard blocker:** Contentful must provide per-environment credentials before the storefront can connect (§6 item 8).
18	- **Read next:** §2 for content types by sprint, §3 for what SFCC consumes, §6 for what must be unblocked before onboarding.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## 0. Purpose & scope [Task-5 framing]
23	
24	**Problem this TSD solves:** give the incoming Contentful squad, and Squad A, a single briefing that pins down the Contentful-to-SFCC integration pattern, the content model SFCC must consume, locale setup, and the SFCC-side build scope, so the two teams share one boundary before the dedicated Contentful squad onboards.
25	
26	- **In scope:** SFCC/MRT-side integration design, content-model requirements SFCC must consume, locale configuration, and the Accenture-vs-Contentful-squad handoff boundary.
27	- **Out of scope:** the full Contentful setup owned by the incoming squad (content authoring, Studio operations, the separate Contentful SOW). Linked, not specified here.
28	
29	Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001): editorial modules, banners, size-guide fallback content, promotional content, and global assets. SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. This spike is the same work item tracked as Open Item #3 ("Define Contentful content model and connector customisation scope") on [TSD: Product, SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061208). Ticket: [SFCC-123](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-123).
30	
31	## 1. Integration architecture & data flow [DoD-1 · Task-1]
32	
33	**Target pattern** (per `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §3-§5 and [Technical Solution Design, PWA](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585) §7): Contentful to MRT (Node/SSR) to browser, SSR-first for SEO and LCP.
34	
35	```
36	PWA (SSR, then CSR hydration)
37	   ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA)      published content, SSR + browser; public token, safe in bundle
38	   ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA)        drafts, MRT proxy only; token server-side, never in browser
39	   ├──► Contentful Images API               images.ctfassets.net, srcset/sizes, AVIF then WebP fallback
40	   ├──► GraphQL Content API                 composed pages, one request, field-projected
41	   └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful   HMAC-verified; clears SSR cache keys
42	```
43	
44	| Surface | Origin / boundary | Token | Notes |
45	|---|---|---|---|
46	| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | SSR-first target; held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
47	| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side) | Studio live preview via iframe `postMessage` |
48	| CMA (schema sync) | CI / local only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Never in MRT or the bundle; build-time only |
49	| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Cache purge; 60s SWR TTL fallback |
50	
51	CDN limit: 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token, absorbed by the SSR cache. Single Contentful Space, one environment per delivery tier (see §4).
52	
53	> **Current implementation vs target (verified in code).** The live data layer is `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`: two hooks (`useContentfulEntry`, `useContentfulEntries`) that fetch **browser-side over REST** from `cdn.contentful.com` (CDA) or `preview.contentful.com` (CPA) with `include=2` to resolve linked assets. Config comes from `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` via `getContentfulConfig()` (which wraps the PWA Kit `ssr-config` `getConfig()`). The **SSR-first fetch, the GraphQL Content API, and the publish-webhook receiver are documented as the target but are not yet in the code** (see §3 and §6, items 3 and 10). This is deliberate build scope, not a defect, but the briefing should not imply SSR editorial is live today.
54	
55	## 2. Content model requirements [DoD-2 · Task-2]
56	
57	**What exists in code today (verified):**
58	
59	- **Studio Experiences** (drag-and-drop, registered via `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react` in `experiences/definitions.ts`, autogenerated from the `.tsx` sources): `collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`.
60	- **CDA content type as schema-as-code** (`scripts/contentful/content-types/`): only `shoppableImage`. Registered in `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` in `contentfulMapping.ts`.
61	- **Editorial React components without a confirmed content type**: `heroBanner`, `duplexSection`, `videoEmbed`, `productHero` (`components/contentful/index.ts`).
62	
63	Contentful integration is not a separate sprint: per `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`, "Contentful works/integration will be done as part of each corresponding functional story." Sprint columns below follow the functional-area schedule (today is Sprint 2, 13-24 Jul).
64	
65	**Required by sprint (Task-2):** Sprint 1 (Homepage & Navigation, Part 1) needs the homepage/navigation editorial types: `collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`, the homepage modules, the navigation / mega menu, the promotional announcement banner, and the global footer. Sprint 2 adds the PLP editorial types (bottom-zone slots and inline grid insert), the PDP size-guide fallback, and the PDP product-information accordion; the SEO FAQ/Article schema sits in the Enhancements backlog. Per each UI story, component shells can be built with mock content ahead of the content model, which is what the "Exists in code?" column reflects. > **DRAFT: Spike SFCC-123.** Working briefing for the incoming Contentful squad, fact-checked against the codebase, Confluence, and Jira as of 22 Jul 2026. Not yet ratified by the squad; open items and the handoff boundary are not final.

# TSD: Contentful Integration, SFCC-Side Design & Content Model (SFCC-123)

> **Status:** In progress · **Owner:** Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz · **Reporter:** Jasmijn Tsang · **Epic:** [SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-1) · **Updated:** 2026-07-22
> **Audience:** the incoming Contentful squad (briefing artefact) plus Squad A engineers building the SFCC-side connection.
> **Provenance:** seeded from the SFCC-123 template and fact-checked against the codebase, Confluence, and the linked Jira stories on 2026-07-22. Items still unconfirmed are called out as open, never asserted as fact.

---

## At a glance

- **What this is:** the SFCC-side briefing for the incoming Contentful squad, covering integration architecture, the content model SFCC must consume, locale setup, and build scope. It is the work tracked as Open Item #3 on the Product TSD.
- **State of play:** the integration is substantially scaffolded (config, data hooks, Studio Experiences, schema-as-code tooling, CSP, CI drift checks), but the SSR-first fetch, the GraphQL Content API, the publish-webhook receiver, and most editorial content types are still to build.
- **Content model today:** one CDA content type (`shoppableImage`) plus three Studio Experiences (`collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`). Everything else in §2 is to build.
- **Locale:** 8 SFCC sites, 10 PWA sites, 9 Contentful locales (`en` default). The earlier count conflict is resolved (§4).
- **Hard blocker:** Contentful must provide per-environment credentials before the storefront can connect (§6 item 8).
- **Read next:** §2 for content types by sprint, §3 for what SFCC consumes, §6 for what must be unblocked before onboarding.

---

## 0. Purpose & scope [Task-5 framing]

**Problem this TSD solves:** give the incoming Contentful squad, and Squad A, a single briefing that pins down the Contentful-to-SFCC integration pattern, the content model SFCC must consume, locale setup, and the SFCC-side build scope, so the two teams share one boundary before the dedicated Contentful squad onboards.

- **In scope:** SFCC/MRT-side integration design, content-model requirements SFCC must consume, locale configuration, and the Accenture-vs-Contentful-squad handoff boundary.
- **Out of scope:** the full Contentful setup owned by the incoming squad (content authoring, Studio operations, the separate Contentful SOW). Linked, not specified here.

Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001): editorial modules, banners, size-guide fallback content, promotional content, and global assets. SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. This spike is the same work item tracked as Open Item #3 ("Define Contentful content model and connector customisation scope") on [TSD: Product, SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061208). Ticket: [SFCC-123](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-123).

## 1. Integration architecture & data flow [DoD-1 · Task-1]

**Target pattern** (per `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §3-§5 and [Technical Solution Design, PWA](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585) §7): Contentful to MRT (Node/SSR) to browser, SSR-first for SEO and LCP.

```
PWA (SSR, then CSR hydration)
   ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA)      published content, SSR + browser; public token, safe in bundle
   ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA)        drafts, MRT proxy only; token server-side, never in browser
   ├──► Contentful Images API               images.ctfassets.net, srcset/sizes, AVIF then WebP fallback
   ├──► GraphQL Content API                 composed pages, one request, field-projected
   └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful   HMAC-verified; clears SSR cache keys
```

| Surface | Origin / boundary | Token | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | SSR-first target; held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side) | Studio live preview via iframe `postMessage` |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI / local only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Never in MRT or the bundle; build-time only |
| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Cache purge; 60s SWR TTL fallback |

CDN limit: 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token, absorbed by the SSR cache. Single Contentful Space, one environment per delivery tier (see §4).

> **Current implementation vs target (verified in code).** The live data layer is `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`: two hooks (`useContentfulEntry`, `useContentfulEntries`) that fetch **browser-side over REST** from `cdn.contentful.com` (CDA) or `preview.contentful.com` (CPA) with `include=2` to resolve linked assets. Config comes from `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` via `getContentfulConfig()` (which wraps the PWA Kit `ssr-config` `getConfig()`). The **SSR-first fetch, the GraphQL Content API, and the publish-webhook receiver are documented as the target but are not yet in the code** (see §3 and §6, items 3 and 10). This is deliberate build scope, not a defect, but the briefing should not imply SSR editorial is live today.

## 2. Content model requirements [DoD-2 · Task-2]

**What exists in code today (verified):**

- **Studio Experiences** (drag-and-drop, registered via `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react` in `experiences/definitions.ts`, autogenerated from the `.tsx` sources): `collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`.
- **CDA content type as schema-as-code** (`scripts/contentful/content-types/`): only `shoppableImage`. Registered in `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` in `contentfulMapping.ts`.
- **Editorial React components without a confirmed content type**: `heroBanner`, `duplexSection`, `videoEmbed`, `productHero` (`components/contentful/index.ts`).

Contentful integration is not a separate sprint: per `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`, "Contentful works/integration will be done as part of each corresponding functional story." Sprint columns below follow the functional-area schedule (today is Sprint 2, 13-24 Jul).

**Required by sprint (Task-2):** Sprint 1 (Homepage & Navigation, Part 1) needs the homepage/navigation editorial types: `collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`, the homepage modules, the navigation / mega menu, the promotional announcement banner, and the global footer. Sprint 2 adds the PLP editorial types (bottom-zone slots and inline grid insert), the PDP size-guide fallback, and the PDP product-information accordion; the SEO FAQ/Article schema sits in the Enhancements backlog. Per each UI story, component shells can be built with mock content ahead of the content model, which is what the "Exists in code?" column reflects. The `Sprint` value in the table is the sprint by which each type is first required.

| Global footer | CMS-managed footer, per-storefront | 1 | No | UI [SFCC-55](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-55) (Tech design) · content [SFCC-117](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-117) (To Do) | to build |

| PLP inline grid insert | Campaign image / image+text / featured tile insert | 2 | No | UI [SFCC-190](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-190) (To Do) · content [SFCC-204](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-204) (To Do) | to build |
| PDP size-guide fallback | Per-product-type size guide slide-out (non-Measmerize) | 2 | No | [SFCC-102](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-102) (In Refinement) | to build (SFCC-owned overlay) |
| PDP product information accordion | Shipping & Returns / Assistance tabs, rich text, per storefront | 2 | No | [SFCC-195](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-195) (In Refinement) | to build |
| SEO FAQ / Article schema | JSON-LD structured data authored in Contentful | Backlog (Enhancements) | No | [SFCC-173](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-173) (To Do) | to build |
| (existing, unmapped) | `productHero`, `videoEmbed` components exist without a confirmed content type | - | Yes (component only) | - | `components/contentful/{productHero,videoEmbed}.tsx` |

**Field reference (verified):**

- `shoppableImage` CDA type: `title` (Symbol, required), `image` (Asset link, required), `imageAlt` (Symbol), `hotspots` (Object; shape `[{ x: 0-100, y: 0-100, productId: "<SFCC master product ID>" }]`). The `productId` key is fixed by `SFCC_PRODUCT_ID_FIELD` in `contentfulMapping.ts`.
- Studio Experience `shoppable-image` stores `hotspots` as a JSON **Text** variable (versus the CDA type's `Object`); worth reconciling to one representation when the model is formalised.
- Studio Experience variables: `collection-hero` (headline, subheadline, ctaLabel, ctaUrl, backgroundImage/Media); `image-text` (image/Media, imageAlt, headline, body, imagePosition default `left`).
- Shoppable-image runtime (verified): `experiences/shoppableImage.tsx` parses the `hotspots` JSON into `{x, y, productId}` markers; `hotspotPopup.tsx` resolves each `productId` through the `useProduct` SCAPI hook (`@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) and renders the SFCC product image (SFCC DIS via `disBaseLink`), name, price, and a PDP link. This is the concrete pattern for Contentful entries that reference SFCC products.

For each **required** type still to build, the incoming squad and Squad A must agree the field set and which fields are localised (`localized: true`) versus structural (`localized: false`, e.g. asset links and product IDs). Schema-as-code lives at `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js`; Studio Experience definitions are generated from `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/*.tsx` via `npm run generate:contentful`.

**Already built (verified against the tree):**

- **Config / types:** `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`, `config/contentfulMapping.ts` + `contentfulMapping.generated.ts` (`SUPPORTED_LOCALES`, `SITE_LOCALES`, `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENTS`, `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS`, `SFCC_PRODUCT_ID_FIELD`), `types/contentful.ts`.

- **Editorial components:** `components/contentful/{heroBanner, duplexSection, videoEmbed, productHero}.tsx`.
- **Studio Experiences:** `components/contentful/experiences/{collectionHero, imageText, shoppableImage, hotspotPopup, hotspotMarker}.tsx` + `definitions.ts`; route `overrides/app/pages/experience/index.tsx`.

## 4. Locale configuration [DoD-3 · Task-4]

**Resolved.** The earlier "locale count" conflict was a category error, not a data conflict:

- **8 SFCC sites / storefront catalogues** (Business Manager view): AU, UK, US, USIntl, EU, EUIntl, HK, ME. The EU site alone carries 5 Business Manager locales (`en`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`), of which the PWA overlay surfaces 4 as single-locale sites; `en` is Business Manager's EU default and is not a separate EU PWA site (ZimmermannEUen uses `en-GB`). - **10 PWA sites, 9 distinct Contentful locales** (`config/sites.overlay.js`, verified): EU domestic is one SFCC site split into four single-locale PWA sites. Distinct locales = `en` (default), `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`. This matches the "9 locales" on the ops page and `DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'en'` in `contentfulMapping.ts`.

> **DRAFT: Spike SFCC-123.** Working briefing for the incoming Contentful squad, fact-checked against the codebase, Confluence, and Jira as of 22 Jul 2026. Not yet ratified by the squad; open items and the handoff boundary are not final.

# TSD: Contentful Integration, SFCC-Side Design & Content Model (SFCC-123)

> **Status:** In progress · **Owner:** Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz · **Reporter:** Jasmijn Tsang · **Epic:** [SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-1) · **Updated:** 2026-07-22
> **Audience:** the incoming Contentful squad (briefing artefact) plus Squad A engineers building the SFCC-side connection.
> **Provenance:** seeded from the SFCC-123 template and fact-checked against the codebase, Confluence, and the linked Jira stories on 2026-07-22. Items still unconfirmed are called out as open, never asserted as fact.

---

## At a glance

- **What this is:** the SFCC-side briefing for the incoming Contentful squad, covering integration architecture, the content model SFCC must consume, locale setup, and build scope. It is the work tracked as Open Item #3 on the Product TSD.
- **State of play:** the integration is substantially scaffolded (config, data hooks, Studio Experiences, schema-as-code tooling, CSP, CI drift checks), but the SSR-first fetch, the GraphQL Content API, the publish-webhook receiver, and most editorial content types are still to build.
- **Content model today:** one CDA content type (`shoppableImage`) plus three Studio Experiences (`collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`). Everything else in §2 is to build.
- **Locale:** 8 SFCC sites, 10 PWA sites, 9 Contentful locales (`en` default). The earlier count conflict is resolved (§4).
- **Hard blocker:** Contentful must provide per-environment credentials before the storefront can connect (§6 item 8).
- **Read next:** §2 for content types by sprint, §3 for what SFCC consumes, §6 for what must be unblocked before onboarding.

---

## 0. Purpose & scope [Task-5 framing]

**Problem this TSD solves:** give the incoming Contentful squad, and Squad A, a single briefing that pins down the Contentful-to-SFCC integration pattern, the content model SFCC must consume, locale setup, and the SFCC-side build scope, so the two teams share one boundary before the dedicated Contentful squad onboards.

- **In scope:** SFCC/MRT-side integration design, content-model requirements SFCC must consume, locale configuration, and the Accenture-vs-Contentful-squad handoff boundary.
- **Out of scope:** the full Contentful setup owned by the incoming squad (content authoring, Studio operations, the separate Contentful SOW). Linked, not specified here.

Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001): editorial modules, banners, size-guide fallback content, promotional content, and global assets. SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. This spike is the same work item tracked as Open Item #3 ("Define Contentful content model and connector customisation scope") on [TSD: Product, SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061208). Ticket: [SFCC-123](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-123).

## 1. Integration architecture & data flow [DoD-1 · Task-1]

**Target pattern** (per `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §3-§5 and [Technical Solution Design, PWA](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585) §7): Contentful to MRT (Node/SSR) to browser, SSR-first for SEO and LCP.

```
PWA (SSR, then CSR hydration)
   ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA)      published content, SSR + browser; public token, safe in bundle
   ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA)        drafts, MRT proxy only; token server-side, never in browser
   ├──► Contentful Images API               images.ctfassets.net, srcset/sizes, AVIF then WebP fallback
   ├──► GraphQL Content API                 composed pages, one request, field-projected
   └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful   HMAC-verified; clears SSR cache keys
```

| Surface | Origin / boundary | Token | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | SSR-first target; held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side) | Studio live preview via iframe `postMessage` |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI / local only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Never in MRT or the bundle; build-time only |
| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Cache purge; 60s SWR TTL fallback |

CDN limit: 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token, absorbed by the SSR cache. Single Contentful Space, one environment per delivery tier (see §4).

> **Current implementation vs target (verified in code).** The live data layer is `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`: two hooks (`useContentfulEntry`, `useContentfulEntries`) that fetch **browser-side over REST** from `cdn.contentful.com` (CDA) or `preview.contentful.com` (CPA) with `include=2` to resolve linked assets. Config comes from `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` via `getContentfulConfig()` (which wraps the PWA Kit `ssr-config` `getConfig()`). The **SSR-first fetch, the GraphQL Content API, and the publish-webhook receiver are documented as the target but are not yet in the code** (see §3 and §6, items 3 and 10). This is deliberate build scope, not a defect, but the briefing should not imply SSR editorial is live today.

## 2. Content model requirements [DoD-2 · Task-2]

**What exists in code today (verified):**

- **Studio Experiences** (drag-and-drop, registered via `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react` in `experiences/definitions.ts`, autogenerated from the `.tsx` sources): `collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`.
- **CDA content type as schema-as-code** (`scripts/contentful/content-types/`): only `shoppableImage`. Registered in `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` in `contentfulMapping.ts`.
- **Editorial React components without a confirmed content type**: `heroBanner`, `duplexSection`, `videoEmbed`, `productHero` (`components/contentful/index.ts`).

Contentful integration is not a separate sprint: per `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`, "Contentful works/integration will be done as part of each corresponding functional story." Sprint columns below follow the functional-area schedule (today is Sprint 2, 13-24 Jul).

**Required by sprint (Task-2):** Sprint 1 (Homepage & Navigation, Part 1) needs the homepage/navigation editorial types: `collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`, the homepage modules, the navigation / mega menu, the promotional announcement banner, and the global footer. Sprint 2 adds the PLP editorial types (bottom-zone slots and inline grid insert), the PDP size-guide fallback, and the PDP product-information accordion; the SEO FAQ/Article schema sits in the Enhancements backlog. Per each UI story, component shells can be built with mock content ahead of the content model, which is what the "Exists in code?" column reflects. The `Sprint` value in the table is the sprint by which each type is first required.

| (existing, unmapped) | `productHero`, `videoEmbed` components exist without a confirmed content type | - | Yes (component only) | - | `components/contentful/{productHero,videoEmbed}.tsx` |

**Field reference (verified):**

- `shoppableImage` CDA type: `title` (Symbol, required), `image` (Asset link, required), `imageAlt` (Symbol), `hotspots` (Object; shape `[{ x: 0-100, y: 0-100, productId: "<SFCC master product ID>" }]`). The `productId` key is fixed by `SFCC_PRODUCT_ID_FIELD` in `contentfulMapping.ts`.
- Studio Experience `shoppable-image` stores `hotspots` as a JSON **Text** variable (versus the CDA type's `Object`); worth reconciling to one representation when the model is formalised.
- Studio Experience variables: `collection-hero` (headline, subheadline, ctaLabel, ctaUrl, backgroundImage/Media); `image-text` (image/Media, imageAlt, headline, body, imagePosition default `left`).
- Shoppable-image runtime (verified): `experiences/shoppableImage.tsx` parses the `hotspots` JSON into `{x, y, productId}` markers; `hotspotPopup.tsx` resolves each `productId` through the `useProduct` SCAPI hook (`@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) and renders the SFCC product image (SFCC DIS via `disBaseLink`), name, price, and a PDP link. This is the concrete pattern for Contentful entries that reference SFCC products.

For each **required** type still to build, the incoming squad and Squad A must agree the field set and which fields are localised (`localized: true`) versus structural (`localized: false`, e.g. asset links and product IDs). Schema-as-code lives at `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js`; Studio Experience definitions are generated from `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/*.tsx` via `npm run generate:contentful`.

| 8 | Per-environment Contentful credentials to be provided (Space ID, environment ID, CDA + CPA tokens, webhook secret) for Dev/QA/SIT/Stage/UAT/Prod; storefront cannot connect without them ([7.1b Third Party Credentials](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/268337165), status: not yet requested) | Zimmermann IT / Contentful | Open, hard blocker |

Code leans SFCC for product images (the shoppable-image popup pulls them from SFCC DIS via `disBaseLink`). Resolve, since it decides whether product imagery is a Contentful concern | Digital / Integration | Open |

## 7. Key design decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Editorial vs commerce ownership | Contentful editorial-only; SFCC owns product, price, inventory | Single source of truth per domain (Product TSD §6, §9) |
| Content types as code | Schema-as-code + typed component, additive-only sync | Reviewable, drift caught at compile time and in CI (PWA TSD §7.3; `02-contentful.md` §2) |
| Studio Experiences | Drag-and-drop components registered via a separate registration module, definitions generated from the `.tsx` sources | Editors compose pages without a deploy (PWA TSD §7.3) |
| SSR-first content fetch (target) | Server-render editorial for SEO/LCP pages | LCP budget; no CDA call on first paint (currently to build, §6 item 10) |
| Content model rides functional stories | No separate Contentful sprint; the content model for each surface ships with its functional story | `sprintScope.md` |

(e) Ownership (`02-contentful.md §1`) marks PLP/PDP editorial split, mega-menu promo tiles, category-landing routing *pending*. (f) Human setup checklist incomplete: MRT env vars per tier, Contentful→MRT cache-purge webhook, Contentful roles, CI CMA GitHub secret. (g) **Hard blocker** (Confluence 268337165): Contentful must provide per-env credentials (Space ID, CDA/CPA tokens, webhook secret). Contentful integration is NOT a separate sprint — it rides each functional story (`.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`). Mapped Contentful stories: SFCC-51 (promo banner, Blocked), 55 (footer), 82/203 (PLP bottom zone), 90 (homepage modules), 102 (PDP size-guide fallback, non-Measmerize), 151 (locale/URL config, 8 storefronts), 173 (SEO FAQ/Article JSON-LD), 190/204 (PLP inline grid insert).

---

**Subject:** New Relic + Sentry — procurement confirmation for PWA observability (SFCC-123)

Hi Emma (cc IT),

Quick one on observability for the SFCC PWA storefront.

Our technical architecture already **designates New Relic (application monitoring + alerting) and Sentry (error tracking) as the observability stack** — the PWA emits per-environment telemetry to both, and the design relies on them to monitor the storefront and raise alerts on incidents (e.g. a CMS/API outage or a failed webhook). This came out of Tim's review of the Contentful integration TSD (SFCC-123): we specify "log the error / alert on the incident," but that needs a confirmed destination.

The tools are **designed-in but not yet procured or tracked**, so before we can wire up monitoring and alerting we need a decision from your side:

1. **Will Zimmermann procure New Relic and Sentry, and who owns the accounts?** (New Relic is the priority per Tim; Sentry is paired with it in our architecture, so same question.)
2. **If yes, we'll need the credentials per environment** (Dev, QA, SIT, Stage, UAT, Prod), which we hold as Managed Runtime (MRT) environment variables on our side:
   - `NEW_RELIC_LICENSE_KEY`
   - `SENTRY_DSN`
   (`ENVIRONMENT_NAME` is set by us — no action needed there.)
3. **Who owns alert/monitor configuration and notifications?** Our expectation: the PWA emits the telemetry, and your team defines the monitors, thresholds, and who gets alerted. Happy to advise on what we emit.
4. **Can we add New Relic and Sentry to the Third Party Credentials tracker** ("7.1b Third Party Credentials") so they're requested through the same channel as the other vendors?

Not urgent for the current build — it's a dependency for **production observability**, not a blocker right now — but we'd like it confirmed and on the tracker well before go-live so it isn't a late surprise.

Happy to jump on a quick call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Marcel

---

content.text:
Audit complete across all three sources. The action item is **directionally correct but was materially imprecise** — New Relic is more decided than "a tool we need to ask about," and the work already has an owner. Here's what validated, what got refined, and what was overstated.

## What I checked
- **Codebase:** `package.json` deps, `.env.sample`, `mobify.config.js`, `ssr.js`/instrumentation, any logger/telemetry util, `architecture.md`.
- **Confluence:** searched the SFCC space for New Relic / Sentry / observability / monitoring / alerting; read PDP integration matrix (257327107) and "12. CDN, eCDN & Security Configuration" (339935324); prior reads of PWA TSD §7 and the credentials tracker (268337165).
- **Jira:** text search across project SFCC for the same terms.

## Claim-by-claim verdict

| Claim in the action item | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Error-handling section raises "log the incident" (CDA-down, HMAC-reject, etc.) | ✅ **Validated** | (b) TSD Error Handling & Monitoring matrix; matches (a) §1 failure modes |
| Tim's answer = an observability tool; ask Emma/IT re New Relic | ✅ **Validated** | the comment itself; New Relic is corroborated as the tool of record |
| New Relic (+ Sentry) already designated in the design | ✅ **Validated** | `architecture.md:108`; PWA TSD §7 env vars; PDP INT-032; Log-Centre routing |
| Not procured / not on the credentials tracker | ✅ **Validated (refined)** | absent from 268337165; open item is literally "**Confirm New Relic licence type**" (PDP INT-032) |
| "no confirmed destination until decided" | ⚠️ **Overstated** | the destination **is** decided — New Relic, per the Accenture **Observability deck** and the SFCC Log-Centre streaming plan; what's pending is the **licence + wiring**, not the choice |

## The true picture (evidence-backed)

1. **New Relic is the decided APM/observability tool**, not a candidate. It's named in `architecture.md`, PWA TSD §7 (`NEW_RELIC_LICENSE_KEY`), the PDP integration matrix (INT-032: "New Relic Browser Agent + server-side MRT instrumentation → performance metrics, error events to New Relic dashboard"), and — the source of truth — an **"Accenture Observability, Tracing & Security Assurance deck"** in the SFCC space that defines the shared-responsibility model and recommends New Relic.
2. **The intended log/alert pipeline exists on paper:** SFCC **Log Centre → stream to New Relic** ("Log Centre Streaming configured to route to the APM destination (New Relic)"), plus MRT request/error/CDN logs streaming. But those checklist items on page 12 are all marked **incomplete** — designed, not yet configured.
3. **It has an owner and a home in Jira:** **SFCC-21 "NFRs & Observability" (Epic, To Do, Squad-B).** So monitoring/alerting is **Squad-B territory under SFCC-21**, not something Squad-A builds into the Contentful TSD.
4. **Zero code yet:** no `newrelic`/`@sentry` deps, no instrumentation — only empty `.env.sample` placeholders (`NEW_RELIC_LICENSE_KEY=`, `SENTRY_DSN=`, `ENVIRONMENT_NAME=`). Pure intent.
5. **Sentry is weaker-attested** than New Relic — only the env placeholder + the `architecture.md` line; it is *not* in the Observability-deck/Log-Centre routing (which names New Relic). So New Relic is the confirmed APM; Sentry is a reserved slot.
6. Nuance: the PDP row marks New Relic "Not Required / P2" — read as "not a PDP-specific integration deliverable" (it's platform-wide APM under SFCC-21), not "New Relic unneeded."

## What this changes for the action (and the message)

The ask to Emma/IT is **narrower and better-anchored** than "will you procure New Relic":
- **Confirm the New Relic licence/plan** ("confirm licence type", browser-agent always-on vs sampled) and procurement owner — reference the **Observability deck** and **SFCC-21**, which already frame it.
- **Get the licence key provisioned** per tier and **Log Centre → New Relic streaming enabled** (the incomplete checklist items on page 12).
- **Confirm the shared-responsibility model** for alert config (likely already in the deck).
- In the Contentful TSD, the incident lines should just **reference New Relic + SFCC Log Centre + SFCC-21**, not redefine monitoring (Tim's scope rule).

So the message I drafted should be **retargeted**: not "which tool," but "New Relic is our recommended APM per the Observability deck — please confirm the licence/procurement and enable Log-Centre streaming," and it should cite SFCC-21 and the deck. Sentry drops to a secondary "also reserved" line.

**Subject:** New Relic observability — licence confirmation + Log Centre streaming (SFCC PWA)

Hi Emma (cc IT),

Following Tim's review of the Contentful TSD (SFCC-123), a quick one to close out observability for the SFCC PWA.

**New Relic is already our chosen APM/observability tool** — it's the recommendation in the Accenture *Observability, Tracing & Security Assurance* deck, it's wired into our architecture (per-tier telemetry tagging), and it's the intended destination for our error/incident logging (e.g. CMS/API outages, failed webhooks). So this isn't a tooling question — it's confirming the licence and switching the pipeline on. This work sits under the **NFRs & Observability epic (SFCC-21)**.

To move it forward we need a few things from your side:

1. **New Relic licence/procurement** — can you confirm Zimmermann's New Relic licence type/plan and who owns the account? (Our open design item is literally "confirm New Relic licence type," incl. whether the browser agent runs always-on or sampled.)
2. **Licence key per environment** — once procured, we'll need `NEW_RELIC_LICENSE_KEY` for each tier (Dev, QA, SIT, Stage, UAT, Prod), which we hold as Managed Runtime (MRT) environment variables.
3. **SFCC Log Centre → New Relic streaming** — this is designed but not yet enabled (Log Centre streaming to the APM destination, plus MRT request/error/CDN logs). Can we get this configured, or agree who owns turning it on?
4. **Alerting ownership** — please confirm the shared-responsibility model for monitors, thresholds, and who receives alerts. Our expectation (and I believe the deck's) is that the PWA emits the telemetry and your team owns alert configuration; happy to walk through what we emit.

Separately, we've also reserved a slot for **Sentry** (error tracking) in the same config — let us know if that's in scope for procurement or something to park for later.

Not blocking the current build — it's a dependency for **production observability** — but we'd like the licence confirmed and Log Centre streaming enabled well before go-live. Happy to jump on a short call, and I can share the Observability deck reference if useful.

Marcel

content.thinking:
The document has evolved significantly to version 15 with substantial revisions from Jhoan and Tim, and there's a new section on SFCC Product & Category ID Reference Patterns in Contentful that wasn't in the earlier version I reviewed.

This new section is a major addition—it documents how SFCC IDs are stored as localized Short Text fields, includes schema-as-code examples, explains render-time resolution in MRT SSR, details cache key requirements, and covers the component contract and null/unscoped behavior. Jhoan explicitly frames this as the core design question the spike was meant to answer, directly addressing Tim's original comment about conditional rendering via SFCC IDs. This is a genuinely substantive solution that draft (a) doesn't have at this depth.

The Error Handling & Monitoring section is heavily reworked with a scope boundary table that clarifies what Squad A/B commits to (null-safe rendering, HMAC, graceful degradation, MRT log drain writing) versus what's out of scope (browser-side New Relic instrumentation) versus recommendations (alert policy creation). It directly addresses the New Relic question by noting that browser-side PWA kit events are out of scope and tracked separately, while the log drain setup is a prerequisite handled elsewhere. A detailed scenario table maps error conditions to handling strategies, logging approaches, incident alerts, and ownership, including specific New Relic alert thresholds like CDA error rate >5% and HMAC violations >3/60s.

There's also a TODO list covering alert thresholds, New Relic notification channels, MRT log drain configuration, browser-layer instrumentation, and Sentry versus New Relic decisions. Jhoan updated the entire section assuming New Relic as the monitoring tool based on the Observability deck, directly addressing action item #2.

The Content Model tables now include SFCC ID patterns across Grid Insert (with sfccCategoryId), PDP Accordion (with sfccProductId and mixed content resolution for Contentful and SFCC tabs), and Returns/Refund messaging (which Jhoan marked as blocked pending the SFCC-14 epic child story). The Handoff Boundary section got retitled and restructured around the Z.immerse ownership split between the Contentful squad and Accenture, though Tim flagged it needs further refinement. ### What's genuinely strong now
- **The new "SFCC Product & Category ID Reference Pattern"** — this is the spike's stated core question (Tim's original "configuring SFCC IDs for conditional rendering"), and (b) answers it well: ShortText `sfccCategoryId`/`sfccProductId` (localized:false), MRT-SSR filtering, cache-key rules, dumb-component contract. This is (b)'s best asset and it's more developed here than in (a).
- **Monitoring scope discipline** — the "commits vs recommendations vs prerequisites" split is honest and useful.
- **Jira mapping breadth** — Sprint-1 types validated against Jira + 04.1.1; the dedicated Contentful stories (SFCC-58/111/117/94/96/195) are correctly captured.
- Duplication trimmed per Tim; Environments-not-Spaces confirmed.

### Flags (ranked, all confirmed against source)

**High — would mislead a reader / self-contradictory:**
1. **CMA-secret status contradiction.** Bootstrap table says "Add CI CMA token as GitHub Actions secret ✅ Complete", but (b)'s own Open Items #4 and Blockers #5 say **Incomplete**, and the ops page (318472193 v7, checklist item 9) says **incomplete**. Three-way contradiction; (b) is wrong vs the source of truth.
2. **Design presented as built.** The "Key behaviours confirmed in 02-contentful.md" list states SSR-first fetch, GraphQL Content API, live preview, and the publish-webhook as current behaviour. Code (`useContentful.ts`) is **browser-side REST only** — no GraphQL, no webhook receiver, no SSR editorial fetch (verified again this pass: no such code, no `@sentry`/`newrelic` deps). A reader will assume these are live.
3. **Locale count still unresolved/contradictory.** Body says "Nine locales"; Blockers #1 still says "confirm the canonical **11-locale set** … 02-contentful.md says 11." Ground truth is **9** (10 PWA sites, `en-AU` is BM's default). (a) resolved this; (b) hasn't.
4. **Sprint-2 table has sprint/epic errors.** It lists **Checkout Trust Messaging (SFCC-67)** and **Returns/Refund (SFCC-14)** as Sprint-2 content types. Per Jira + `sprintScope.md`, checkout is **Sprint 4**, returns is **Sprint 7**, and **SFCC-14 is an Epic**. (b) fixed the epic note in the capability table but not in the Sprint-2 table.

**Medium:**
5. **Handoff Boundary is knowingly unfinished** — literally titled "**[FOR UPDATE]**"; Tim: "this table is not quite right, I will update." That's the DoD's core "brief the incoming squad on the boundary" section.
6. **SFCC-ID pattern is 100% design, with a gap and a naming mismatch.** No `sfccCategoryId`/`sfccProductId` exists in code (verified). It's presented as "resolved design" but doesn't flag **Tim's explicitly-required feasibility spike** (comment 352124930: "we need a spike … capture the # in the SFCC PLP … test item counts and pagination"). Also proposes `sfccProductId` while the one existing field is `productId` (`SFCC_PRODUCT_ID_FIELD`).
7. **Monitoring section cites the wrong source.** Jhoan grounded the New-Relic rewrite in `A4BOEg` = the **draft "Integration Reconciliation" working doc**, which marks New Relic **"Not Required."** The authoritative recommendation is the **Accenture Observability, Tracing & Security Assurance deck** (referenced on page 339935324). New Relic is still the right tool — but the citation undercuts the section.
8. **Product-image ownership stated as settled** ("SFCC BM static content library") while PWA TSD §9 says Contentful and the **DC002 decision page is empty/undecided**. Asserts a call that isn't made.

**Low:**
9. **Broken self-link** — the "Tell No Lies" link (Didomi scenario + monitoring) points to `.../x/BoCrF`, i.e. **this page itself**.
10. **Cache concern only half-addressed** — the new cache-key section handles ID-collision correctness, but Tim's actual worry (footer/homepage always render from Contentful → CDA-hit frequency) is met with "risk accepted: bare render is visually broken," which sits in tension with the "graceful degradation, never block" principle. Worth an explicit position.

### Cross-source alignment
- **Codebase:** "Already built" inventory is accurate; the architecture "confirmed behaviours" and the SFCC-ID pattern are **not in code** (flags 2, 6).
- **Confluence:** contradicts the ops page on the CMA secret (flag 1); New-Relic basis is a draft doc that says "Not Required" (flag 7); the cited doc itself notes Confluence is stale on Contentful vs the repo.
- **Jira:** mostly correct mappings; Sprint-2 sprint/epic errors remain (flag 4).

### Open Tim threads still live in-doc
Handoff table (he'll update); cache re-think (partially addressed); PLP-inject pagination spike (flagged to Hazel, not yet a card); PDP-accordion mixed-content spike (flagged); Sprint-2 authoring session with Emma & Dani (not yet done).

### Verdict
**Standing: strong working draft, not sign-off-ready.** It now covers all four DoD pillars and uniquely nails the SFCC-ID conditional-rendering design, but four high-severity items — the CMA-secret contradiction, the built-vs-target overstatement, the unresolved locale count, and the Sprint-2 sprint/epic errors — plus the "[FOR UPDATE]" handoff mean it would mislead the incoming squad if shared as-is. All are quick fixes. Closest path to done: resolve those four, re-source the New-Relic section to the Observability deck, add the two flagged spikes as cards, and finish the handoff table.

Want me to (a) turn this into a comment set to drop on the page for Jhoan/Tim, (b) fix the items that overlap with (a) so the two docs stop diverging, or (c) just hand you the ranked flag list to raise verbally?

    "type": "page",
