    "content": {
      "value": "Overview
--------

Editorial and CMS content in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team. MRT (Managed Runtime — Salesforce's PWA hosting layer) acts as the integration layer between Contentful and the browser-rendered PWA storefront.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Direction** | **Flow** |
| Inbound (Contentful → MRT) | Published content entries (hero banners, editorial modules, navigation, footer, announcement banners, size guides, accordion copy) delivered via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA) to the MRT SSR layer on every page render. |
| Outbound (MRT → Contentful) | Cache-purge webhook acknowledgements; Management API calls from CI for schema migrations. No content flows from SFCC back to Contentful. |
| NOT in this flow | SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly. All CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. |

*Contentful is the sole CMS for all eight Zimmermann storefronts. SFCC manages commerce data (products, pricing, orders); Contentful manages editorial data (copy, imagery configuration, page layouts). They complement each other without overlap.*

Integration Architecture & Data Flow
------------------------------------

**Pattern:** Contentful → MRT (Node/SSR) → browser, SSR-first for SEO/LCP.

### Architecture diagram

wide760PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
│
├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
│ SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
│ post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
│
├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
│ Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
│ never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
│ an MRT preview endpoint.
│
├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
│ srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
│
└──◄ Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
HMAC-verified with a shared secret.

### **API surface & token boundary**

| Surface | Origin / Boundary | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | SSR-first; browser hydrates from SSR payload. Safe to embed in bundle. |
| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side) | Editor preview via iframe `postMessage`. Never reaches browser. |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI host only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Never in MRT/bundle — build-time only. Never embedded, never in PR diffs. |
| Publish webhook | Contentful → MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish. TTL fallback 60s SWR. Rejected and logged if HMAC fails. |

**Key behaviours confirmed in** `02-contentful.md`**:**

* **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
* **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries, the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
* **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
* **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint. `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head.
* **SSR cache TTL.** 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache — the TTL is the fallback if a webhook drops.
* **CDN rate limit.** 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic — risk only during burst republish events.
* **Bundle weight.** Rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
* **No PII** flows through Contentful.

### Content Ownership (from 02-contentful.md)

SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001).

| **Surface** | **SFCC Owns** | **Contentful Owns** | **Status** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
| Size guides | — | Fallback content only. Primary size guide is Measmerize overlay (PRD-053). Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists. | Confirmed |
| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | Pending — whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful |
| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary is Measmerize — PRD-053) | Pending — which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer |
| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | Pending |
| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005) | — | Confirmed — Contentful is not the source of badge content |

SFCC Product & Category ID Reference Pattern in Contentful
----------------------------------------------------------

This section documents the resolved design for how SFCC product and category IDs are embedded in Contentful content models, how MRT resolves them at render time, and how conditional component rendering is implemented based on those IDs. This is the core design question the spike(SFCC-123) was tasked to answer.

### Content Model: How to Store SFCC IDs

SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain Short Text fields on the Contentful content type. They are not localized — they are structural fields that identify what SFCC data the editorial entry is associated with, and the value does not change per locale.

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Field Name** | **Field Type** | **Localized** | **Applies To** | **Description** |
| sfccCategoryId | Short Text | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | The SFCC category ID (e.g. womens-dresses) this entry is scoped to. If null, the entry is shown on all categories of that type. |
| sfccProductId | Short Text | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | The SFCC product ID (master product ID) this entry is scoped to. If null, shown on all PDPs. |
| sfccProductIds | Short Text (list) | No | Campaign editorial, Homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. |
| sfccCategoryIds | Short Text (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. |

*Authoring rule: content authors set sfccCategoryId / sfccProductId in Contentful. They do not need to know anything about how MRT resolves it — that logic lives entirely in the SSR layer.*

### Schema-as-Code Definition

Each content type that supports ID-based targeting must include the relevant field in its scripts/contentful/content-types/\*.js definition. Example for PLP Inline Grid Insert:

wide760true{
id: 'sfccCategoryId',
name: 'SFCC Category ID',
type: 'Symbol',          // Short Text in Contentful UI
localized: false,
required: false,
validations: []
}

### Render-Time Resolution in MRT (SSR)

At SSR time, MRT fetches all published entries of a given content type for the current locale via CDA. Before passing entries to React components, the SSR layer filters them by matching the SFCC ID field against the current page context. The component never sees unmatched entries — it receives only the entries that should render.

**Resolution logic by page context:**

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Page Context** | **ID Source** | **Match Logic** |
| PLP (category page) | Route param / SFCC category API response | Filter CDA entries where sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId OR sfccCategoryId is null (show-on-all). |
| PDP (product page) | Route param productId (master product ID) | Filter CDA entries where sfccProductId === currentProductId OR sfccProductId is null. |
| Homepage | No SFCC ID context | No ID filtering — all entries for the slot are rendered in authored order. |
| Campaign landing | Slug / experience ID | Filtered by Contentful Studio Experience — no SFCC ID filtering needed. |

**Pseudocode — MRT SSR filter (PLP example):**

const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({   content\_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert',   locale: currentLocale, });  const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter(entry => {   const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields;   // null = show on all categories; specific ID = scoped render   return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId; });  // Only matched entries are passed to the component return <PlpInlineGridInsert entries={matchedInserts} />;

### Cache Key Requirements

This is a critical implication of the ID-based filtering pattern. If SSR cache keys do not include the SFCC category or product ID, the cached response for one category will be incorrectly served to a different category.

*Cache key rule: any page whose SSR output depends on sfccCategoryId filtering MUST include the category ID in its MRT cache key. Same rule applies to sfccProductId on PDPs. Failure to do this will cause editorial components to appear on the wrong category/product pages.*

**Cache key construction:**

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Page** | **Cache Key Must Include** |
| PLP | locale + categoryId + (page number if paginated) |
| PDP | locale + productId |
| Homepage | locale only (no SFCC ID context) |

### Component Contract

React components that render SFCC-ID-targeted content must be written to the following contract:

* The component does NOT receive raw Contentful entries — it receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer.
* The component does NOT contain any SFCC ID comparison logic.
* The component renders all entries it receives, in the order it receives them.
* If the entries array is empty (no match), the component renders nothing — null return, no DOM output.

This keeps the component reusable across different SFCC ID scopes without modification.

### Null / Unscoped Behaviour

A Contentful entry with sfccCategoryId = null (field left empty by the author) is treated as "show on all categories" for that content type. This is the default authoring state. Authors only populate the ID field when they want to restrict the component to a specific category or product.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **sfccCategoryId value** | **Render behaviour** |
| null (empty) | Show on all PLPs of this content type |
| "womens-dresses" | Show only on the womens-dresses PLP |
| "mens-shirts" | Show only on the mens-shirts PLP |

**Environment & Locale Configuration**
--------------------------------------

The platform uses a single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev → test → sit → staging → uat → production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias (`CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production`) for zero-downtime releases. Nine locales are configured across eight storefronts, with `en` as the default fallback. Full environment setup, alias management, and locale configuration are maintained in Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations.

### Locale Rules for Content Modellers

* Translatable fields (headline, body copy, CTA text, alt text) → set localized: true in the content type definition.
* Structural fields (asset links, layout flags, product IDs) → set localized: false — shared across all locales. Canonical examples of non-localized structural fields: sfccCategoryId and sfccProductId. These are SFCC identifiers and do not vary by locale.
* Fallback chain: if a locale (e.g. fr) has no content for a field, Contentful falls back to en automatically. Authors only fill fields they want to override.
* Translation pipeline: Transperfect is the translation partner (HPC-006). Strategy is under discussion — Contentful squad to own.

Key Design Decisions
--------------------

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Decision** | **Choice** | **Rationale** |
| Single Contentful Space for all 8 storefronts | One Space, per-locale content fields | Locale model handles per-storefront variation. Avoids content duplication and reduces operational overhead vs one space per storefront. |
| Schema as code — not hand-created in UI | Git-managed definitions deployed via npm run sync:contentful | Prevents schema drift, enables code review of content model changes, and gives CI visibility of structural changes before production. |
| CDA token in browser bundle (delivery only) | Delivery API token is browser-safe | CDA tokens are read-only and scoped to one environment. Preview (CPA) and Management (CMA) tokens are never deployed to MRT or exposed to the browser. |
| Production alias instead of fixed environment name | CONTENTFUL\_ENVIRONMENT\_ID=production resolves to an alias | Enables zero-downtime releases: flip the alias to a pre-tested release clone without redeploying MRT. Requires Contentful Enterprise plan. |
| ISR cache invalidation via webhook on publish | Contentful fires HMAC-signed webhook → MRT invalidates cache | Pages are server-rendered and cached. Without cache invalidation, published content changes would not appear until cache TTL expires. Webhook makes updates near-real-time. |
| Graceful degradation for CMS unavailability | Render page without editorial content if Contentful is down | Commerce functionality must never be blocked by CMS availability. Editorial content is an enhancement, not a dependency. |
| Contentful SDK v11 — no connection pool isolation hook | Mitigate via graceful degradation, not pool isolation | SDK v11 does not expose a dispatcher hook for custom connection pooling. Primary mitigation is graceful degradation. |
| SFCC ID references in Contentful content model | Plain ShortText fields (sfccProductId, sfccCategoryId), localized: false. Filtering in MRT SSR, not in the React component. | ID fields are structural, not editorial — they do not vary by locale. Resolution and conditional rendering happen entirely in the MRT SSR layer. The Contentful entry is the editorial shell; SFCC provides the commerce data it wraps. Components remain dumb and reusable. Cache keys must include the SFCC ID to avoid cross-context cache collisions. |

Overview

Editorial and CMS content in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team. MRT (Managed Runtime — Salesforce's PWA hosting layer) acts as the integration layer between Contentful and the browser-rendered PWA storefront.

Direction

Flow

Inbound (Contentful → MRT)

Published content entries (hero banners, editorial modules, navigation, footer, announcement banners, size guides, accordion copy) delivered via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA) to the MRT SSR layer on every page render.

Outbound (MRT → Contentful)

Cache-purge webhook acknowledgements; Management API calls from CI for schema migrations. No content flows from SFCC back to Contentful.

NOT in this flow

SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly. All CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager.

Contentful is the sole CMS for all eight Zimmermann storefronts. SFCC manages commerce data (products, pricing, orders); Contentful manages editorial data (copy, imagery configuration, page layouts). They complement each other without overlap.

Integration Architecture & Data Flow

Pattern: Contentful → MRT (Node/SSR) → browser, SSR-first for SEO/LCP.

Architecture diagram

Key behaviours confirmed in 02-contentful.md:

  • SSR first. Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.

  • GraphQL for composed pages. Where a page assembles many entries, the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.

  • Live preview. When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on postMessage events from Studio.

  • Asset delivery. Images come from images.ctfassets.net. The storefront generates srcset, sizes, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint. images.ctfassets.net is preconnected from the document head.

  • SSR cache TTL. 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache — the TTL is the fallback if a webhook drops.

  • CDN rate limit. 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic — risk only during burst republish events.

  • Bundle weight. Rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.

  • No PII flows through Contentful.

SFCC Product & Category ID Reference Pattern in Contentful

This section documents the resolved design for how SFCC product and category IDs are embedded in Contentful content models, how MRT resolves them at render time, and how conditional component rendering is implemented based on those IDs. This is the core design question the spike(SFCC-123) was tasked to answer.

Content Model: How to Store SFCC IDs

SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain Short Text fields on the Contentful content type. They are not localized — they are structural fields that identify what SFCC data the editorial entry is associated with, and the value does not change per locale.

Field Name

Field Type

Localized

Applies To

Description

sfccCategoryId

Short Text

No

PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles

The SFCC category ID (e.g. womens-dresses) this entry is scoped to. If null, the entry is shown on all categories of that type.

sfccProductId

Short Text

No

PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look

The SFCC product ID (master product ID) this entry is scoped to. If null, shown on all PDPs.

sfccProductIds

Short Text (list)

No

sfccCategoryIds

Short Text (list)

No

Authoring rule: content authors set sfccCategoryId / sfccProductId in Contentful. They do not need to know anything about how MRT resolves it — that logic lives entirely in the SSR layer.

Schema-as-Code Definition

Each content type that supports ID-based targeting must include the relevant field in its scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js definition. Example for PLP Inline Grid Insert:

wide760true

Render-Time Resolution in MRT (SSR)

At SSR time, MRT fetches all published entries of a given content type for the current locale via CDA. Before passing entries to React components, the SSR layer filters them by matching the SFCC ID field against the current page context. The component never sees unmatched entries — it receives only the entries that should render.

Resolution logic by page context:

Page Context

ID Source

Match Logic

PLP (category page)

Route param / SFCC category API response

Filter CDA entries where sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId OR sfccCategoryId is null (show-on-all).

PDP (product page)

Route param productId (master product ID)

Filter CDA entries where sfccProductId === currentProductId OR sfccProductId is null.

Homepage

No SFCC ID context

No ID filtering — all entries for the slot are rendered in authored order.

Campaign landing

Slug / experience ID

Filtered by Contentful Studio Experience — no SFCC ID filtering needed.

Pseudocode — MRT SSR filter (PLP example):

const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({   content_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert',   locale: currentLocale, });  const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter(entry => {   const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields;   // null = show on all categories; specific ID = scoped render   return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId; });  // Only matched entries are passed to the component return <PlpInlineGridInsert entries={matchedInserts} />;

Cache Key Requirements

This is a critical implication of the ID-based filtering pattern. If SSR cache keys do not include the SFCC category or product ID, the cached response for one category will be incorrectly served to a different category. 

Cache key rule: any page whose SSR output depends on sfccCategoryId filtering MUST include the category ID in its MRT cache key. Same rule applies to sfccProductId on PDPs. Failure to do this will cause editorial components to appear on the wrong category/product pages.

Cache Key Must Include

locale + categoryId + (page number if paginated)

PDP

locale + productId

Homepage

locale only (no SFCC ID context)

Component Contract

React components that render SFCC-ID-targeted content must be written to the following contract:

  • The component does NOT receive raw Contentful entries — it receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer.

  • The component does NOT contain any SFCC ID comparison logic.

  • The component renders all entries it receives, in the order it receives them.

  • If the entries array is empty (no match), the component renders nothing — null return, no DOM output.

This keeps the component reusable across different SFCC ID scopes without modification.

Null / Unscoped Behaviour

A Contentful entry with sfccCategoryId = null (field left empty by the author) is treated as "show on all categories" for that content type. This is the default authoring state. Authors only populate the ID field when they want to restrict the component to a specific category or product.

Environment & Locale Configuration

The platform uses a single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev → test → sit → staging → uat → production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias (CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production) for zero-downtime releases. Nine locales are configured across eight storefronts, with en as the default fallback. Full environment setup, alias management, and locale configuration are maintained in Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations.

Locale Rules for Content Modellers

  • Translatable fields (headline, body copy, CTA text, alt text) → set localized: true in the content type definition.

  • Structural fields (asset links, layout flags, product IDs) → set localized: false — shared across all locales. Canonical examples of non-localized structural fields: sfccCategoryId and sfccProductId. These are SFCC identifiers and do not vary by locale.

  • Fallback chain: if a locale (e.g. fr) has no content for a field, Contentful falls back to en automatically. Authors only fill fields they want to override.

  • Translation pipeline: Transperfect is the translation partner (HPC-006). Strategy is under discussion — Contentful squad to own.

Key Design Decisions

Decision

Choice

Rationale

Single Contentful Space for all 8 storefronts

One Space, per-locale content fields

Locale model handles per-storefront variation. Avoids content duplication and reduces operational overhead vs one space per storefront.

Schema as code — not hand-created in UI

Prevents schema drift, enables code review of content model changes, and gives CI visibility of structural changes before production.

CDA token in browser bundle (delivery only)

Delivery API token is browser-safe

CDA tokens are read-only and scoped to one environment. Preview (CPA) and Management (CMA) tokens are never deployed to MRT or exposed to the browser.

Production alias instead of fixed environment name

CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production resolves to an alias

Enables zero-downtime releases: flip the alias to a pre-tested release clone without redeploying MRT. Requires Contentful Enterprise plan.

ISR cache invalidation via webhook on publish

Contentful fires HMAC-signed webhook → MRT invalidates cache

Pages are server-rendered and cached. Without cache invalidation, published content changes would not appear until cache TTL expires. Webhook makes updates near-real-time.

Graceful degradation for CMS unavailability

Render page without editorial content if Contentful is down

Commerce functionality must never be blocked by CMS availability. Editorial content is an enhancement, not a dependency.

Contentful SDK v11 — no connection pool isolation hook

Mitigate via graceful degradation, not pool isolation

SDK v11 does not expose a dispatcher hook for custom connection pooling. Primary mitigation is graceful degradation.

SFCC ID references in Contentful content model

Plain ShortText fields (sfccProductId, sfccCategoryId), localized: false. Filtering in MRT SSR, not in the React component.

ID fields are structural, not editorial — they do not vary by locale. Resolution and conditional rendering happen entirely in the MRT SSR layer. The Contentful entry is the editorial shell; SFCC provides the commerce data it wraps. Components remain dumb and reusable. Cache keys must include the SFCC ID to avoid cross-context cache collisions.

content.text:
Here's the reasoning behind each item so you can hold the line in a review. First the through-line, because it's your strongest defense of the whole set.

## The big picture (what almost every finding actually is)

Two themes run through all 14:
- **"The doc says X, but the source says Y."** The TSD claims things the codebase, Jira, or the ops runbook contradict (or the doc contradicts itself). These aren't opinions - they're verifiable in about a minute each.
- **"This is written as decided, but it isn't."** A few things are stated as settled fact when the decision hasn't been made (or belongs to someone else).

So when you defend it: none of this is style nitpicking. It's either a factual mismatch or an unmade decision presented as made. A TSD's job is to be the thing the incoming squad can trust and build against - both themes break that.

I've tagged each item as **[Fact]** (not debatable, source wins), **[Risk]** (don't lock something unproven), or **[Decision]** (needs a lead/PO, not us).

---

## Fix before we share

**1. CMA-token status contradiction — [Fact]**
- **Conflict:** The same task is "Complete" in the Bootstrap table but "Incomplete" in Blockers #5, Open Items #4, and the ops runbook (page 318472193, item 9). That token is what lets CI run `sync/migrate:contentful` - so it's not cosmetic; it says whether the content pipeline actually works.
- **Options:** mark incomplete everywhere / mark complete everywhere / leave contradictory (not viable).
- **Why our pick (reconcile to incomplete unless confirmed):** three places including the source-of-truth runbook say incomplete; the lone "Complete" is the outlier. Under-claim beats over-claim on readiness.
- **Defense:** "A TSD can't say a task is both done and not-done. The ops runbook is the setup source of truth and says incomplete. If it's actually done, a 2-minute check with the Integration Lead settles it - but it has to be one value."

**2. SSR / GraphQL / webhook shown as built — [Fact], highest-impact**
- **Conflict:** The architecture section states SSR-first editorial fetch, GraphQL, live preview, and the publish webhook as current behaviour, and lists the data hook under "Already built." The code does none of it: `useContentful.ts` is client-side React hooks hitting the REST CDA/CPA; the experience route also fetches client-side (Spinner while loading); there is no GraphQL client, no server-side Contentful fetch anywhere (nothing in `ssr.js`, no `getProps` pulls Contentful), and no `/webhooks/contentful` receiver.
- **Options:** (a) split "built today" vs "target, to build"; (b) actually build SSR/GraphQL/webhook (real engineering, not a doc edit); (c) leave it (misleads).
- **Why our pick (a):** the squad plans against this doc. If they think SSR editorial + webhook cache-purge are done, they'll assume SEO/LCP and near-real-time updates are handled - all unbuilt. Labeling target vs built costs nothing and turns an overstatement into a clean build backlog.
- **Defense:** This is the one most likely to get pushback ("02-contentful.md describes it that way"). Counter: 02-contentful.md is the *target* integration guide; the TSD copied it as *current*. The proof is in the repo - open `useContentful.ts` (it's `useEffect`+`fetch`), grep for a webhook route (none), grep for graphql (none). Tim already probed this instinct ("where are we logging this and how?"). You're not saying the target is wrong, you're saying don't describe it as done.

**3. Locale count 9 vs 11 — [Fact]**
- **Conflict:** Body says nine locales (right); Blocker #1 still says "confirm the canonical 11-locale set." The doc states 9 and flags 11 as unresolved at the same time.
- **Substance:** three counts got tangled - 8 = SFCC sites, 9 = Contentful locales, 10 = PWA sites. "11" was a stale line in 02-contentful.md that wrongly counted `en-AU` (BM's AU default, which the PWA narrows to `en`) plus a duplicate EU `en`.
- **Options:** close as resolved (9) / keep it open as "confirm 11" (wrong - answer is known).
- **Why our pick:** `config/sites.overlay.js` (10 sites → 9 distinct locales) and the ops page both say 9. Code wins. Leaving it "open" fabricates a blocker for locale bootstrap.
- **Defense:** "It's not 8 vs 9 vs 11 - those count different things. The 9 is code-verified and matches the ops runbook; the 11 was a stale doc line. Nothing to confirm."

**4. Sprint-2 table has Sprint-4/7 items and an Epic — [Fact]**
- **Conflict:** Sprint-2 content types list Checkout Trust Messaging (SFCC-67) and Returns/Refund (SFCC-14). Jira: SFCC-67's parent epic is Checkout Flow & Delivery (Sprint 4); SFCC-14 is the Returns & Refunds **Epic** (Sprint 7). You don't "build to" an epic - you build to its child stories.
- **Implication:** Sprint-2 is meant to say "what you need now." Padding it with Sprint-4/7 work inflates immediate scope and could trigger building content types months early.
- **Options:** move to correct sprints (+ reference SFCC-14's child story when it exists) / leave (wrong scope).
- **Why our pick:** Jira + the sprint plan are the source of truth, and Tim already made the epic point in a comment. Jhoan half-fixed it (capability table now notes the epic) but the Sprint-2 table still lists both.
- **Defense:** "Straight from Jira and the sprint plan, and Tim already flagged the epic. We're not dropping them, just filing them under the sprint they belong to."

**5. Handoff Boundary still "[FOR UPDATE]" — [Decision, Tim]**
- **Conflict:** The section that tells the incoming squad what Accenture builds vs what they own is literally marked "[FOR UPDATE]," and the Z.immerse ownership rows are muddled. That boundary IS the DoD ("brief the squad on where their remit starts").
- **Options:** finalise before sharing / share unfinished (defeats the purpose).
- **Why our pick:** Tim self-assigned the update ("I will update"). Sharing a half-done ownership table to an external squad creates exactly the confusion the doc exists to prevent.
- **Defense:** "This one's a sequencing dependency on Tim, not a Jhoan task - he owns the rewrite. We just don't share until it's done."

---

## Validate before finalising

**6. Sprint-2 content types are assumed, not confirmed — [Risk]**
- **Conflict:** Field sets for SFCC-82/190/67 are inferred from UI descriptions; the real content-model stories don't exist, and none map to a 04.1.1 HPC requirement. Jhoan flagged this herself.
- **Implication:** Lock guessed fields → the squad models the wrong schema → migrations + re-authoring later (expensive once content exists).
- **Options:** confirm with the content owners (Emma/Dani) first / lock now and risk rework / mark provisional.
- **Why our pick (mark provisional + book the session):** Tim explicitly asked to "run the authoring approach by Emma and Dani," and Jhoan agreed the set is assumed.
- **Defense:** "This is Tim's ask and Jhoan's own flag. A short session with the content authors de-risks a costly content-model rework."

**7. Mega Menu fields are design-dependent — [Risk]**
- **Conflict:** The nav content model depends on the SFCC-96 Figma, which isn't delivered.
- **Why our pick (mark provisional pending Figma):** you don't finalise a content model for a design-driven component before the design exists, or the fields won't match (promo tiles, editorial slots).
- **Defense:** Low controversy - Jhoan already noted it; SFCC-96 is design-dependent in Jira.

---

## Spikes and to-dos to raise (not blocking)

**8. PLP inline insert - injection into the SFCC grid — [Risk], the meaty one**
- **Conflict:** The doc presents "inject a Contentful editorial tile into the SFCC PLP product grid, scoped by category ID" as resolved design. Tim flagged the real unknown: an SFCC PLP is a **paginated product-search result**, and inserting a non-product tile can break the item count ("24 of 240"), page boundaries, and load-more math.
- **Options & implications:** (a) interleave server-side into the result set - clean UX but this is the thing that can corrupt counts/pagination; (b) overlay the tile as a grid cell client-side after the product fetch - safer for counts, trickier for layout/position; (c) accept the design as-is and find out at build time (worst).
- **Why our pick (mark "pending feasibility spike" + raise the card):** the pattern is sound in principle (SSR filter by category ID), but the grid-injection mechanics are genuinely unproven, and it may force approach (a) vs (b). Tim said exactly this.
- **Defense:** "The pattern's fine; the open question is whether injecting into SFCC's paginated grid breaks counts/pagination - which is an SFCC quirk, not a Contentful one. Tim raised it. Flagging it as spike-pending protects the estimate; we're not reworking the design, we're proving one mechanic."

**9. PDP accordion mixed content — [Risk]**
- **Conflict:** One accordion mixes Contentful tabs (Shipping & Returns, Assistance) with SFCC-sourced tabs (Details & Care, Size & Fit); exact SFCC fields and the render approach are TBD (Tim asked "simple SFCC var or a dedicated component?"). The card is still In Refinement.
- **Why our pick (raise the spike):** mixing two data sources with different rendering (rich text vs product attributes) in one component is a real integration question; don't lock it before proving it.
- **Defense:** Same logic as #8, and again it's Tim's own question. Card's In Refinement, so the fields aren't final anyway.

**10. MRT-apps section — [scope hygiene, agreed]**
- **Conflict:** The TSD carries MRT-app content that Tim said belongs in a separate TSD (yours + Gideon's).
- **Why our pick (scratch + link once the separate TSD exists):** no point deleting content with nowhere to point yet; sequence it.
- **Defense:** Already agreed across you, Jhoan, and Tim. Just closing the loop.

---

## Raise with leads / POs (decisions outside our control)

**11. New Relic - wrong source + not procured — [Decision + Fact]**
- **Conflict:** Two parts. (a) The monitoring rewrite is anchored to the "Integration Reconciliation working doc," which is a *draft* that actually lists New Relic as **"Not Required."** So the section justifies New Relic with a source that says the opposite. The real basis is the Accenture Observability, Tracing & Security Assurance deck (referenced from page 339935324, which also holds the Log Centre → New Relic streaming checklist). (b) New Relic is designed-in (env var, checklist) but not procured or on the credentials tracker, so the alert policies are aspirational.
- **Options:** re-anchor to 339935324/the deck + frame alerts as "recommended, pending procurement" / leave citing the draft (weak, self-contradicting).
- **Why our pick:** New Relic IS the right, decided tool (the deck + the architecture back it) - only the citation and the readiness framing are off. You're separately driving procurement with Emma/IT.
- **Defense:** "The tool choice is fine - it's in the Observability deck and the architecture. But we can't justify it by citing a draft that says 'Not Required'; anchor to 339935324. And since it's not bought yet, the alerts are 'recommended, pending procurement.'" This actually pre-empts Tim's classic "is this procured, who owns alerts?"

**12. Product-image ownership asserted vs undecided — [Decision]**
- **Conflict:** The doc states "product imagery lives in SFCC BM" as fact under "What is NOT in Contentful." But it's undecided: the PWA TSD says all imagery is served from Contentful, the Product TSD says product images load into SFCC, and the dedicated decision page **DC002 is empty**. Code leans SFCC (the shoppable-image popup pulls product images from SFCC DIS), but that's evidence, not a ruling.
- **Options:** mark "pending DC002" + escalate / assert SFCC (risk being wrong; then the "not in Contentful" scope is wrong and asset handling gets mis-planned).
- **Why our pick:** two TSDs conflict and the decision page is empty - that is, by definition, undecided.
- **Defense:** "We have two TSDs saying opposite things and an empty DC002. The code leaning SFCC is a hint, not a decision. This is a Digital/Integration + PO call - the TSD can't declare it. I'll push for the DC002 ruling."

**13. Cache / graceful degradation stance — [Decision]**
- **Conflict:** The doc's principle is "Contentful is an enhancement, never block/never break." But footer and homepage are 100% Contentful-driven, so a full CDA outage yields a visibly broken page - which the doc currently just calls "risk accepted." Those two statements can't both be true. Tim raised the underlying cache concern.
- **Options & implications:** (a) accept Contentful as a hard dependency for that chrome and lean on the SSR cache serving **last-known-good/stale** during an outage (degrades to slightly stale, not blank); (b) build minimal static fallbacks (footer links, homepage skeleton) - more work, fully resilient; (c) "accept the risk" (current - not actually a design position).
- **Why our pick (take a firm position with Tim, likely serve stale-cached rather than blank):** "risk accepted" is a shrug that contradicts the never-break principle stated elsewhere. Stale-while-revalidate already exists in the design, so serving the last good footer/homepage during an outage is the low-cost, defensible stance.
- **Defense:** "It's Tim's cache concern, and it's an internal contradiction: we say 'never break the page' then accept a broken page. We don't have to prescribe the fix, but the team needs a real degradation stance - serving stale-cached chrome beats a blank render."

---

## Minor

**14. "Tell No Lies" link points to itself — [Fact]**
- **Conflict:** A link labeled "Tell No Lies" (the GTM/analytics vendor) actually links back to this same TSD page (the `x/BoCrF` tiny link). Copy-paste slip.
- **Why our pick (repoint or drop):** it's just wrong.
- **Defense:** None needed - self-referential link, obvious mistake.

---

## How to defend the whole thing in one breath
- **Not debatable (source wins):** 1, 3, 4, 14 - the code, Jira, or ops runbook say so; the doc just needs to match.
- **Risk management (don't lock the unproven):** 2, 6, 7, 8, 9 - label target-vs-built and spike-pending so nobody builds to a guess.
- **Not our call (needs a lead/PO):** 5 (Tim), 11 (Emma/IT + deck), 12 (DC002/PO), 13 (Tim).

And the meta-rebuttal if someone calls it nitpicking: **the four high-severity ones (1-4) would actively mislead the incoming squad about what's built, how many locales exist, and what's due this sprint - that's the exact opposite of what a briefing artefact is for.** Everything else is either de-risking or routing a decision to its owner.

Both checks landed real findings — item 2 got an extra concrete example, and item 3 turned out to be a genuinely bigger story than "one stale line." Here's what I found, then the rewritten items.

## Item 2 — re-verified

Confirmed again, plus a stronger example: it's not just the experience route — the **actual homepage** (`overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx`) also pulls Contentful content via the same client-side `useContentfulEntries`/`useContentfulEntry` hooks (plus `useContentfulLiveUpdates` for live preview). No GraphQL client, no webhook route/handler anywhere in `overrides/` or `scripts/`. So the finding holds, and now has a more concrete citation than before.

## Item 3 — this needed real digging, and the story changed

My earlier "the 11 is a stale line" was too thin. Here's what's actually going on:

- **The built/live state is 9** — confirmed by `contentfulMapping.generated.ts` (auto-generated from live SFCC), `sites.overlay.js` (10 PWA sites → 9 locale codes), the ops runbook, and the TSD's own body text. Consistent across four independent places.
- **"11" isn't a typo — it's a genuine conflation, traced to its source.** It comes from the Regional Storefronts PRD (REG-043). That PRD's own table has **11 rows** — but two locale codes are each shared by two rows (`en-GB` for UK *and* EU-domestic-EN; `en-US` for US domestic *and* the planned US-international site). Count the distinct codes in that same table and you get **9**, not 11. So "11 active locales" in the PRD (and the two other docs that copy it) is actually counting **storefront rows**, not distinct locales.
- **One of those 11 rows doesn't exist in code yet.** The 11th row is a planned US-international split (REG-005, updated 2026-07-10, site ID `ZimmermannUSIntl` still marked **TBC** in the PRD itself) — it's a real, dated decision, but it hasn't landed in `sites.overlay.js`. And per the PRD's own mapping, that new site would reuse the `en-US` locale anyway — so even once built, the distinct-locale count stays 9.
- **Bonus find:** `02-contentful.md`'s specific locale list is wrong on its own terms too — it says "Eleven active locales" but only lists 10 codes, one of which (`en-AU`) isn't real (AU's actual Contentful locale is bare `en`).

So this isn't "9 is right, 11 is a mistake to dismiss" — it's "9 is the correct count for what's built and live today; 11 comes from a real but differently-scoped PRD requirement (site count, including a not-yet-built site) that's been miscopied as a locale count." Worth a quick confirm with whoever owns REG-005/the regional config, since it's a dated, active decision, not dead text.

Can we confirm the actual state and make it consistent - if the CI CMA secret has genuinely been added, tick it everywhere and update the runbook; if not, mark it Incomplete?

      "value": "Overview
--------

Editorial and CMS content in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team. MRT (Managed Runtime — Salesforce's PWA hosting layer) acts as the integration layer between Contentful and the browser-rendered PWA storefront.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Direction** | **Flow** |
| Inbound (Contentful → MRT) | Published content entries (hero banners, editorial modules, navigation, footer, announcement banners, size guides, accordion copy) delivered via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA). Target: fetched server-side by the MRT SSR layer. Current: fetched client-side post-hydration. |
| Outbound (MRT → Contentful) | Cache-purge webhook acknowledgements; Management API calls from CI for schema migrations. No content flows from SFCC back to Contentful. |
| NOT in this flow | SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly. All CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. |

*Contentful is the sole CMS for all eight Zimmermann storefronts. SFCC manages commerce data (products, pricing, orders); Contentful manages editorial data (copy, imagery configuration, page layouts). They complement each other without overlap.*

Integration Architecture & Data Flow
------------------------------------

**Pattern:** Contentful → MRT (Node/SSR) → browser.

### Architecture diagram

wide760PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
│
├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
│ SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
│ post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
│
├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
│ Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
│ never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
│ an MRT preview endpoint.
│
├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
│ srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
│
└──◄ Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
HMAC-verified with a shared secret.

### **API surface & token boundary**

| Surface | Origin / Boundary | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | Safe to embed in bundle. |
| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side) | Editor preview via iframe `postMessage`. Never reaches browser. |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI host only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Never in MRT/bundle — build-time only. Never embedded, never in PR diffs. |
| Publish webhook | Contentful → MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish. TTL fallback 60s SWR. Rejected and logged if HMAC fails. |

#### Current state (built today)

These are confirmed by the code in the repo as of this spike.

| What | File | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CDA fetch hook | `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | `useContentfulEntries` and `useContentfulEntry` — **client-side only** (`useEffect`). Fires in the browser after hydration, not during SSR. |
| Homepage Contentful fetch | `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` | Calls `useContentfulEntries('homepage')` in `HomeNormal` — CSR via `useEffect`. |
| Live preview (Studio) | `pages/home/index.tsx` + `useContentfulLiveUpdates` | Preview path wired via `?entry=` param. Uses `@contentful/live-preview/react`. |
| Editorial components | `overrides/app/components/contentful/` | `heroBanner`, `productHero`, `duplexSection`, `videoEmbed` |
| Studio Experience components | `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/` | `CollectionHero`, `ImageText`, `ShoppableImage` registered via `definitions.ts` |
| Studio Experience route | `overrides/app/pages/experience/index.tsx` | — |
| Config & types | `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`, `config/contentfulMapping.ts`, `types/contentful.ts` | Token config resolved from MRT `getConfig()` |
| Schema-as-code tooling | `scripts/contentful/sync.js`, `generateDefinitions.mjs`, `migrations/`, `setup/bootstrapSpace.mjs` | — |
| CSP allowances | `overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts` | `cdn.contentful.com`, `preview.contentful.com`, `images.ctfassets.net`, `frame-ancestors: app.contentful.com` |

#### Target architecture (to build)

These are the intended production patterns. **None of these exist in the codebase yet.** Squads must not assume they are live.

| What | Why it's needed | Build reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SSR-first CDA fetch | Editorial content for SEO/LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP) must be fetched server-side. Currently `useContentful.ts` fires in the browser — first paint shows a spinner, not content. Target: SSR fetches CDA, browser hydrates from SSR payload with no CDA call on first paint. | Replace `useEffect` fetch with server-side data loading in the MRT SSR layer. |
| GraphQL Content API | For composed pages that assemble multiple entries, a single GraphQL query fetches only the needed fields, avoiding multiple REST round-trips and over-fetching. Currently all fetches use REST CDA (`cdn.contentful.com/.../entries`). | Introduce a GraphQL client (e.g. `graphql-request`) and query layer per content type. |
| HMAC-verified publish webhook receiver | When an editor publishes in Contentful Studio, the MRT SSR cache must be purged immediately. Without this, content changes won't appear until the 60s TTL expires. Currently no webhook endpoint exists in `overrides/` or `scripts/`. | Build a `POST /webhooks/contentful` handler in the MRT Node layer. Verify `X-Contentful-Signature` against `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. |

### Content Ownership (from 02-contentful.md)

SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001).

| **Surface** | **SFCC Owns** | **Contentful Owns** | **Status** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
| Size guides | — | Fallback content only. Primary size guide is Measmerize overlay (PRD-053). Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists. | Confirmed |
| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | Pending — whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful |
| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary is Measmerize — PRD-053) | Pending — which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer |
| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | Pending |
| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005) | — | Confirmed — Contentful is not the source of badge content |

SFCC Product & Category ID Reference Pattern in Contentful
----------------------------------------------------------

This section documents the resolved design for how SFCC product and category IDs are embedded in Contentful content models, how MRT resolves them at render time, and how conditional component rendering is implemented based on those IDs. This is the core design question the spike(SFCC-123) was tasked to answer.

### Content Model: How to Store SFCC IDs

SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain Short Text fields on the Contentful content type. They are not localized — they are structural fields that identify what SFCC data the editorial entry is associated with, and the value does not change per locale.

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Field Name** | **Field Type** | **Localized** | **Applies To** | **Description** |
| sfccCategoryId | Short Text | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | The SFCC category ID (e.g. womens-dresses) this entry is scoped to. If null, the entry is shown on all categories of that type. |
| sfccProductId | Short Text | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | The SFCC product ID (master product ID) this entry is scoped to. If null, shown on all PDPs. |
| sfccProductIds | Short Text (list) | No | Campaign editorial, Homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. |
| sfccCategoryIds | Short Text (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. |

*Authoring rule: content authors set sfccCategoryId / sfccProductId in Contentful. They do not need to know anything about how MRT resolves it — that logic lives entirely in the SSR layer.*

### Schema-as-Code Definition

Each content type that supports ID-based targeting must include the relevant field in its scripts/contentful/content-types/\*.js definition. Example for PLP Inline Grid Insert:

wide760true{
id: 'sfccCategoryId',
name: 'SFCC Category ID',
type: 'Symbol',          // Short Text in Contentful UI
localized: false,
required: false,
validations: []
}

### Render-Time Resolution in MRT (SSR)

At SSR time, MRT fetches all published entries of a given content type for the current locale via CDA. Before passing entries to React components, the SSR layer filters them by matching the SFCC ID field against the current page context. The component never sees unmatched entries — it receives only the entries that should render.

**Resolution logic by page context:**

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Page Context** | **ID Source** | **Match Logic** |
| PLP (category page) | Route param / SFCC category API response | Filter CDA entries where sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId OR sfccCategoryId is null (show-on-all). |
| PDP (product page) | Route param productId (master product ID) | Filter CDA entries where sfccProductId === currentProductId OR sfccProductId is null. |
| Homepage | No SFCC ID context | No ID filtering — all entries for the slot are rendered in authored order. |
| Campaign landing | Slug / experience ID | Filtered by Contentful Studio Experience — no SFCC ID filtering needed. |

**Pseudocode — MRT SSR filter (PLP example):**

const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({   content\_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert',   locale: currentLocale, });  const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter(entry => {   const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields;   // null = show on all categories; specific ID = scoped render   return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId; });  // Only matched entries are passed to the component return <PlpInlineGridInsert entries={matchedInserts} />;

### Cache Key Requirements

This is a critical implication of the ID-based filtering pattern. If SSR cache keys do not include the SFCC category or product ID, the cached response for one category will be incorrectly served to a different category.

*Cache key rule: any page whose SSR output depends on sfccCategoryId filtering MUST include the category ID in its MRT cache key. Same rule applies to sfccProductId on PDPs. Failure to do this will cause editorial components to appear on the wrong category/product pages.*

**Cache key construction:**

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Page** | **Cache Key Must Include** |
| PLP | locale + categoryId + (page number if paginated) |
| PDP | locale + productId |
| Homepage | locale only (no SFCC ID context) |

### Component Contract

React components that render SFCC-ID-targeted content must be written to the following contract:

* The component does NOT receive raw Contentful entries — it receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer.
* The component does NOT contain any SFCC ID comparison logic.
* The component renders all entries it receives, in the order it receives them.
* If the entries array is empty (no match), the component renders nothing — null return, no DOM output.

This keeps the component reusable across different SFCC ID scopes without modification.

### Null / Unscoped Behaviour

A Contentful entry with sfccCategoryId = null (field left empty by the author) is treated as "show on all categories" for that content type. This is the default authoring state. Authors only populate the ID field when they want to restrict the component to a specific category or product.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **sfccCategoryId value** | **Render behaviour** |
| null (empty) | Show on all PLPs of this content type |
| "womens-dresses" | Show only on the womens-dresses PLP |
| "mens-shirts" | Show only on the mens-shirts PLP |

**Environment & Locale Configuration**
--------------------------------------

The platform uses a single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev → test → sit → staging → uat → production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias (`CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production`) for zero-downtime releases. Nine locales are configured across eight storefronts, with `en` as the default fallback. Full environment setup, alias management, and locale configuration are maintained in Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations.

### Locale Rules for Content Modellers

* Translatable fields (headline, body copy, CTA text, alt text) → set localized: true in the content type definition.
* Structural fields (asset links, layout flags, product IDs) → set localized: false — shared across all locales. Canonical examples of non-localized structural fields: sfccCategoryId and sfccProductId. These are SFCC identifiers and do not vary by locale.
* Fallback chain: if a locale (e.g. fr) has no content for a field, Contentful falls back to en automatically. Authors only fill fields they want to override.
* Translation pipeline: Transperfect is the translation partner (HPC-006). Strategy is under discussion — Contentful squad to own.

Key Design Decisions
--------------------

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Decision** | **Choice** | **Rationale** |
| Single Contentful Space for all 8 storefronts | One Space, per-locale content fields | Locale model handles per-storefront variation. Avoids content duplication and reduces operational overhead vs one space per storefront. |
| Schema as code — not hand-created in UI | Git-managed definitions deployed via npm run sync:contentful | Prevents schema drift, enables code review of content model changes, and gives CI visibility of structural changes before production. |
| CDA token in browser bundle (delivery only) | Delivery API token is browser-safe | CDA tokens are read-only and scoped to one environment. Preview (CPA) and Management (CMA) tokens are never deployed to MRT or exposed to the browser. |
| Production alias instead of fixed environment name | CONTENTFUL\_ENVIRONMENT\_ID=production resolves to an alias | Enables zero-downtime releases: flip the alias to a pre-tested release clone without redeploying MRT. Requires Contentful Enterprise plan. |
| ISR cache invalidation via webhook on publish | Contentful fires HMAC-signed webhook → MRT invalidates cache | Pages are server-rendered and cached. Without cache invalidation, published content changes would not appear until cache TTL expires. Webhook makes updates near-real-time. |
| Graceful degradation for CMS unavailability | Render page without editorial content if Contentful is down | Commerce functionality must never be blocked by CMS availability. Editorial content is an enhancement, not a dependency. |
| Contentful SDK v11 — no connection pool isolation hook | Mitigate via graceful degradation, not pool isolation | SDK v11 does not expose a dispatcher hook for custom connection pooling. Primary mitigation is graceful degradation. |
| SFCC ID references in Contentful content model | Plain ShortText fields (sfccProductId, sfccCategoryId), localized: false. Filtering in MRT SSR, not in the React component. | ID fields are structural, not editorial — they do not vary by locale. Resolution and conditional rendering happen entirely in the MRT SSR layer. The Contentful entry is the editorial shell; SFCC provides the commerce data it wraps. Components remain dumb and reusable. Cache keys must include the SFCC ID to avoid cross-context cache collisions. |

Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001). It manages editorial content,
banners, size guides, promotional content, and global assets. Integration is via the Contentful Delivery
API (CDA) for all customer-facing pages, with the Contentful Preview API (CPA) available server-side only.

**Architecture:** Single Contentful space with one environment per delivery tier.
Environment IDs match SFCC tier names exactly — no mapping required at runtime.

Environment Topology
--------------------

Six-tier delivery pipeline. Contentful environment IDs map directly to MRT push targets.

| Tier | Name | Contentful Env ID | MRT Push Command | MRT URL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 & 2 | DEV | `dev` | `npm run push:dev` | zimmermann-dev.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |

| 7 | PRODUCTION | `master` (via `production` alias) | `npm run push:prod` | zimmermann-production.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |

Promotion order: **dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master**

Alias Strategy & Release Workflow
---------------------------------

Two aliases are maintained and always kept in sync:

* `production` — what MRT production tier uses (`CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production`). Flipping this is the zero-downtime release mechanism.
* `master` — Contentful’s built-in alias, kept in sync with `production`.

### Release workflow

1. Create a release environment in the Contentful web UI: clone from the current `production` target, name it `release-YYYY-MM`.
2. Run migrations: `npm run migrate:contentful -- --target release-YYYY-MM`
3. Test against the release environment directly (bypasses the alias).
4. Promote: `npm run promote:alias -- --target release-YYYY-MM` (flips both aliases atomically).
5. Retain the previous environment for 14 days as a rollback target, then delete.

The `production` alias requires the Contentful Enterprise plan. The `master` alias is always available as the built-in fallback.

API Keys & Tokens
-----------------

| Variable | Scope | Local .env | GitHub Actions | MRT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` | Space (shared) | ✓ | Variable | ✓ per tier |

| `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Per env, read-only | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |

| `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Per user (personal) | ✓ | Secret (CI service account) | **Never** |
| `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Per env | ✓ | Secret per env | ✓ per tier |

### CI service account CMA token

Create a dedicated Contentful user (e.g. `contentful-ci@zimmermann.com`), invite as Space Administrator,
log in as that user and generate a Personal Access Token under Account Settings → CMA Tokens.
Store as the `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` GitHub Actions secret.

### Per-developer setup

Each developer generates their own CMA token: **Contentful → top-right avatar → Account Settings → CMA Tokens → Create personal access token**.
Add it to local `.env` as `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`. Delivery and preview tokens are space-level — run `npm run config:contentful` to populate them automatically.

Locale Configuration
--------------------

Nine locales matching SFCC `config/sites.js` exactly. No runtime mapping required.

| Locale Code | Name | Storefront(s) | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `en` | English (AU) | ZimmermannAU | Default |
| `en-US` | English (US) | ZimmermannUS | en |
| `en-GB` | English (UK / EU) | ZimmermannUK, ZimmermannEUen | en |
| `fr` | French | ZimmermannEUfr | en |

| `en-HK` | English (HK) | ZimmermannHK | en |
| `en-AE` | English (ME) | ZimmermannME | en |

Locales are created in the `master` environment during bootstrap; cloned environments inherit them automatically. All translatable fields use `localized: true`; structural fields (asset links, product IDs) use `localized: false`.

Content Type Management
-----------------------

|  | Editorial content types | Studio Experiences definitions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Location** | `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/*ContentfulDefinition.ts` |

content.text:
Checked — the evidence is decisive. **"Not yet resolved" is correct; "resolved" is the error.**

**Evidence:**
- **Jira:** No spike or story exists for the mixed-content question. Search for "accordion"/"mixed content" across the whole SFCC project returns only SFCC-195 itself (still **In Refinement**), two unrelated design subtasks (SFCC-207/209, about accordion tab *UI* layout, not data-source resolution), and unrelated stories. No card resolves this.
- **Comments:** Both Tim (351830036 — "something we may want to investigate, if it's just a simple SFCC var or a dedicated component") and Jhoan herself (354713614 — "I do suggest to have a spike for mixed content rendering") describe this as an open question, not something decided.
- **Codebase:** There is **no PDP accordion component built yet** anywhere in `overrides/` (the only "accordion" hits are translation-string files with the tab labels, not logic). And there's **no OCAPI-based content fetch anywhere** — the only OCAPI references in the repo are legacy config/env-switching residue, and two other docs explicitly call OCAPI **deprecated**, with SCAPI as its replacement. So the "resolved via SFCC Open Commerce API" claim isn't just unbuilt — it proposes building new functionality on an API the project has already moved away from.

So the fix direction is confirmed: walk the **Content Model Requirements → Sprint 2 table** back to match the (correct) Capability Build Table language:

**Revised (item #3, confirmed direction):**
> Mixed content resolution (Contentful tabs + SFCC tabs) **proposed, not yet resolved**: Contentful tabs (Shipping & Returns, Assistance) render via rich-text renderer; SFCC tabs (Details & Care, Size & Fit) are SFCC-sourced — **exact rendering mechanism (simple SFCC variable call vs. dedicated component) and the API to use are still TBC, pending a spike (no card raised yet — see Capability Build Table).**

Worth flagging in the same note: the specific "SFCC Open Commerce API" detail should be dropped entirely rather than carried into the walked-back version — citing OCAPI at all risks steering the eventual spike toward a deprecated API when SCAPI is the project's stated direction.

    "type": "page",

    "content": {
      "value": "Overview
--------

Editorial and CMS content in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team. MRT (Managed Runtime — Salesforce's PWA hosting layer) acts as the integration layer between Contentful and the browser-rendered PWA storefront.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Direction** | **Flow** |
| Inbound (Contentful → MRT) | Published content entries (hero banners, editorial modules, navigation, footer, announcement banners, size guides, accordion copy) delivered via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA). Target: fetched server-side by the MRT SSR layer. Current: fetched client-side post-hydration. |
| Outbound (MRT → Contentful) | Cache-purge webhook acknowledgements; Management API calls from CI for schema migrations. No content flows from SFCC back to Contentful. |
| NOT in this flow | SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly. All CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. |

*Contentful is the sole CMS for all eight Zimmermann storefronts. SFCC manages commerce data (products, pricing, orders); Contentful manages editorial data (copy, imagery configuration, page layouts). They complement each other without overlap.*

Integration Architecture & Data Flow
------------------------------------

**Pattern:** Contentful → MRT (Node/SSR) → browser.

### Architecture diagram

wide760PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
│
├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
│ SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
│ post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
│
├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
│ Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
│ never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
│ an MRT preview endpoint.
│
├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
│ srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
│
└──◄ Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
HMAC-verified with a shared secret.

### **API surface & token boundary**

| Surface | Origin / Boundary | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | Safe to embed in bundle. |
| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side) | Editor preview via iframe `postMessage`. Never reaches browser. |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI host only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Never in MRT/bundle — build-time only. Never embedded, never in PR diffs. |
| Publish webhook | Contentful → MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Clears SSR cache keys on publish. TTL fallback 60s SWR. Rejected and logged if HMAC fails. |

#### Current state (built today)

These are confirmed by the code in the repo as of this spike.

| What | File | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CDA fetch hook | `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | `useContentfulEntries` and `useContentfulEntry` — **client-side only** (`useEffect`). Fires in the browser after hydration, not during SSR. |
| Homepage Contentful fetch | `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` | Calls `useContentfulEntries('homepage')` in `HomeNormal` — CSR via `useEffect`. |
| Live preview (Studio) | `pages/home/index.tsx` + `useContentfulLiveUpdates` | Preview path wired via `?entry=` param. Uses `@contentful/live-preview/react`. |
| Editorial components | `overrides/app/components/contentful/` | `heroBanner`, `productHero`, `duplexSection`, `videoEmbed` |
| Studio Experience components | `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/` | `CollectionHero`, `ImageText`, `ShoppableImage` registered via `definitions.ts` |
| Studio Experience route | `overrides/app/pages/experience/index.tsx` | — |
| Config & types | `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`, `config/contentfulMapping.ts`, `types/contentful.ts` | Token config resolved from MRT `getConfig()` |
| Schema-as-code tooling | `scripts/contentful/sync.js`, `generateDefinitions.mjs`, `migrations/`, `setup/bootstrapSpace.mjs` | — |
| CSP allowances | `overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts` | `cdn.contentful.com`, `preview.contentful.com`, `images.ctfassets.net`, `frame-ancestors: app.contentful.com` |

#### Target architecture (to build)

These are the intended production patterns. **None of these exist in the codebase yet.** Squads must not assume they are live.

| What | Why it's needed | Build reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SSR-first CDA fetch | Editorial content for SEO/LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP) must be fetched server-side. Currently `useContentful.ts` fires in the browser — first paint shows a spinner, not content. Target: SSR fetches CDA, browser hydrates from SSR payload with no CDA call on first paint. | Replace `useEffect` fetch with server-side data loading in the MRT SSR layer. |
| GraphQL Content API | For composed pages that assemble multiple entries, a single GraphQL query fetches only the needed fields, avoiding multiple REST round-trips and over-fetching. Currently all fetches use REST CDA (`cdn.contentful.com/.../entries`). | Introduce a GraphQL client (e.g. `graphql-request`) and query layer per content type. |
| HMAC-verified publish webhook receiver | When an editor publishes in Contentful Studio, the MRT SSR cache must be purged immediately. Without this, content changes won't appear until the 60s TTL expires. Currently no webhook endpoint exists in `overrides/` or `scripts/`. | Build a `POST /webhooks/contentful` handler in the MRT Node layer. Verify `X-Contentful-Signature` against `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. |

### Content Ownership (from 02-contentful.md)

SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001).

| **Surface** | **SFCC Owns** | **Contentful Owns** | **Status** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
| Size guides | — | Fallback content only. Primary size guide is Measmerize overlay (PRD-053). Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists. | Confirmed |
| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | Pending — whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful |
| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary is Measmerize — PRD-053) | Pending — which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer |
| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | Pending |
| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005) | — | Confirmed — Contentful is not the source of badge content |

SFCC Product & Category ID Reference Pattern in Contentful
----------------------------------------------------------

This section documents the resolved design for how SFCC product and category IDs are embedded in Contentful content models, how MRT resolves them at render time, and how conditional component rendering is implemented based on those IDs. This is the core design question the spike(SFCC-123) was tasked to answer.

### Content Model: How to Store SFCC IDs

SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain Short Text fields on the Contentful content type. They are not localized — they are structural fields that identify what SFCC data the editorial entry is associated with, and the value does not change per locale.

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Field Name** | **Field Type** | **Localized** | **Applies To** | **Description** |
| sfccCategoryId | Short Text | No | PLP editorial slots, Inline Grid Insert, Mega Menu tiles | The SFCC category ID (e.g. womens-dresses) this entry is scoped to. If null, the entry is shown on all categories of that type. |
| sfccProductId | Short Text | No | PDP editorial blocks, Shop the Look | The SFCC product ID (master product ID) this entry is scoped to. If null, shown on all PDPs. |
| sfccProductIds | Short Text (list) | No | Campaign editorial, Homepage personalisation | Array of SFCC product IDs when an entry targets multiple products. |
| sfccCategoryIds | Short Text (list) | No | Multi-category editorial slots | Array of SFCC category IDs when an entry targets multiple categories. |

*Authoring rule: content authors set sfccCategoryId / sfccProductId in Contentful. They do not need to know anything about how MRT resolves it — that logic lives entirely in the SSR layer.*

### Schema-as-Code Definition

Each content type that supports ID-based targeting must include the relevant field in its scripts/contentful/content-types/\*.js definition. Example for PLP Inline Grid Insert:

wide760true{
id: 'sfccCategoryId',
name: 'SFCC Category ID',
type: 'Symbol',          // Short Text in Contentful UI
localized: false,
required: false,
validations: []
}

### Render-Time Resolution in MRT (SSR)

At SSR time, MRT fetches all published entries of a given content type for the current locale via CDA. Before passing entries to React components, the SSR layer filters them by matching the SFCC ID field against the current page context. The component never sees unmatched entries — it receives only the entries that should render.

**Resolution logic by page context:**

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Page Context** | **ID Source** | **Match Logic** |
| PLP (category page) | Route param / SFCC category API response | Filter CDA entries where sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId OR sfccCategoryId is null (show-on-all). |
| PDP (product page) | Route param productId (master product ID) | Filter CDA entries where sfccProductId === currentProductId OR sfccProductId is null. |
| Homepage | No SFCC ID context | No ID filtering — all entries for the slot are rendered in authored order. |
| Campaign landing | Slug / experience ID | Filtered by Contentful Studio Experience — no SFCC ID filtering needed. |

**Pseudocode — MRT SSR filter (PLP example):**

const allGridInserts = await contentfulClient.getEntries({   content\_type: 'plpInlineGridInsert',   locale: currentLocale, });  const matchedInserts = allGridInserts.items.filter(entry => {   const { sfccCategoryId } = entry.fields;   // null = show on all categories; specific ID = scoped render   return !sfccCategoryId || sfccCategoryId === currentCategoryId; });  // Only matched entries are passed to the component return <PlpInlineGridInsert entries={matchedInserts} />;

### Cache Key Requirements

This is a critical implication of the ID-based filtering pattern. If SSR cache keys do not include the SFCC category or product ID, the cached response for one category will be incorrectly served to a different category.

*Cache key rule: any page whose SSR output depends on sfccCategoryId filtering MUST include the category ID in its MRT cache key. Same rule applies to sfccProductId on PDPs. Failure to do this will cause editorial components to appear on the wrong category/product pages.*

**Cache key construction:**

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Page** | **Cache Key Must Include** |
| PLP | locale + categoryId + (page number if paginated) |
| PDP | locale + productId |
| Homepage | locale only (no SFCC ID context) |

### Component Contract

React components that render SFCC-ID-targeted content must be written to the following contract:

* The component does NOT receive raw Contentful entries — it receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer.
* The component does NOT contain any SFCC ID comparison logic.
* The component renders all entries it receives, in the order it receives them.
* If the entries array is empty (no match), the component renders nothing — null return, no DOM output.

This keeps the component reusable across different SFCC ID scopes without modification.

### Null / Unscoped Behaviour

A Contentful entry with sfccCategoryId = null (field left empty by the author) is treated as "show on all categories" for that content type. This is the default authoring state. Authors only populate the ID field when they want to restrict the component to a specific category or product.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **sfccCategoryId value** | **Render behaviour** |
| null (empty) | Show on all PLPs of this content type |
| "womens-dresses" | Show only on the womens-dresses PLP |
| "mens-shirts" | Show only on the mens-shirts PLP |
